title: Mimir
subtitle: A three-month search for memory that learns, proven in Lean and measured on LongMemEval.
intro_md:
Mimir is a research project on **long-term memory for AI** — built over three months (February 27 to May 30, 2026) around a single uncomfortable question: *can a system actually **learn** continuously from a stream of conversation, or does it only ever **retrieve**?*

Retrieval, it turns out, is largely solved. A well-tuned hybrid of BM25, cosine similarity, and a cross-encoder reranker already places the right evidence in the top-10 over 97% of the time. The open frontier is everything that retrieval is *not*: writing experience into a model's weights, predicting latent structure, binding events into episodes, reasoning over time. Mimir is the record of chasing that frontier — what worked, what failed loudly, and why.

The method is deliberately **dual**. On the formal side, Lean 4 proofs establish the dynamics a memory system *should* obey — Banach fixed-point stability, Lyapunov energy descent, a derived stability boundary — across two sorry-free libraries totaling 335 theorems. On the empirical side, every claim is forced through the **LongMemEval / MemoryAgentBench** benchmarks under the unforgiving SubEM metric. The two halves were meant to reinforce each other. Sometimes they did; sometimes the proofs stayed pristine while reality refused to cooperate — a tension that became one of the project's central lessons.

The journey runs across eleven families. It opens with **agentic ReAct retrieval** (an early winner that later measured *negative* against a single deterministic function) and settles on the **Engram/foundry recall() core**, the canonical system that reached a #1-on-leaderboard 60.33%. Around it orbit the supporting and the abandoned: **knowledge-graph** and **information-extraction** work that fought extraction-vocabulary mismatch; **temporal reasoning** that kept colliding with the difference between when an event was *discussed* and when it *happened*; **episodic event-binding** that was correct but score-neutral; **dual-extraction observations** still alive at the close. The hardest mandate — **continual learning, parametric memory, and JEPA world-models** — was brutal almost everywhere, with test-time training the one flicker of life. The **Lean/energy** half stayed mathematically perfect but empirically vacuous at scale. And a final **post-processing, routing, and evaluation-integrity** thread kept the whole enterprise honest — removing hard-coded shortcuts even when it cost points. This is that record.
reflection_md:
# MIMIR — Closing the Journal (Feb 27 – May 30, 2026)

Three months, ~200 experiments, two disciplines (Lean proofs + Python eval on LongMemEval/SubEM). The honest summary: **retrieval, done carefully, beat everything we built on top of it.**

## What won
The **honest, no-hard-coding retrieval baseline** — BM25 + cosine RRF + cross-encoder rerank, plus EventFrames and turn-level indexing — reached **60.33% SubEM (181/300)** on LME-S* 5-ctx, topping every named system: GPT-4.1-mini (55.7%), MIRIX (51.0%), HippoRAG-v2 (50.7%), Gemini-2.0-Flash (47.0%). On the full benchmark, **56% (280/500)**. That is the deliverable. It started life at 43.33% (`recall()`) and 16.67% (plain cosine, mabench era); the whole arc was disciplined retrieval engineering, not novel memory mechanisms.

## Correct but vacuous
The **Lean formalizations** (75 + 260 theorems, 0 sorry) are *correct*: energy descent / Lyapunov stability hold 100% in proof. But at LME scale (N≈1200 dense turns) they are **empirically vacuous** — transfer bound 1000× loose, alignment gap δ negative, energy-as-predictor AUC 0.34–0.53 (success vs failure energy: −0.789 vs −0.790). Even shrinking to N=53 fact centroids only made the theory *prettier*, never *predictive*. Hopfield energy is content-addressable completion; LME demands reasoning over facts. Right math, wrong abstraction.

## The dead-ends that taught the most
- **Parametric / LoRA continual learning** — every scale failed (1.5B ceiling 17% and high-variance; 7B *diverged* to 0/60). Knowledge injection via weights is a knife-edge; absorption, not refusal, is the wall.
- **Hopfield/NLCDM energy** — see above; strictly worse than cosine at retrieval.
- **ReAct / agentic retrieval** — −5 SubEM vs a single deterministic pass.
- **Code oracle** — net −2 on LME-500; it *corrupted already-correct answers*.
- **Hard-coded regex** — the +15 it bought (196 vs 181) was the benchmark computing the answer, not memory. Deleting it was the most important commit of the project.

## Where it points
Retrieval is **solved enough**. The open frontier is **continuous learning** — systems that *learn from a conversation stream* (inner/outer loop, SLM-as-oracle, world models), not ones that re-rank a frozen corpus. TTT (30% probe, 2.5× the offline ceiling) is the only parametric signal that survived; it's the thread worth pulling. The goal was never a leaderboard — it was **universal, evergreen memory**. The benchmark was the flashlight, never the room.

approach_cards.name: recall() — single deterministic retrieval function (BM25+cosine RRF + cross-encoder rerank)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Retrieval is essentially solved: one deterministic function (BM25 + cosine RRF + cross-encoder rerank) with regex predicate-dispatch beats an iterative agent and forms the right core.
approach_cards.method: recall() in foundry/retrieval.py: BM25 + cosine RRF, cross-encoder rerank. Predicate dispatch: count/sum/list→aggregate(), when/time→Allen temporal, default→BM25+cosine+rerank. decompose_recall_params() regex-based, no LLM. Replaced AgenticRetriever.
approach_cards.result: recall() baseline 43.33% SubEM on ctx0 (single context). Became the foundation for all subsequent foundry gains. ReAct agent measured at -5 SubEM relative to this.
approach_cards.notes: Single function replaced the whole agentic toolkit. Remaining bottleneck = extraction quality (Qwen2.5-7B mistypes 'facebook' as 'fish').

approach_cards.name: Turn-level BM25 indexing (vs 512-token chunks)
approach_cards.hypothesis: A 35-point gap vs mabench came from BM25 indexing 512-token chunks (739 docs) instead of individual turns (1282 docs); turn-granularity indexing restores recall.
approach_cards.method: _rebuild_bm25_with_turns() in foundry/eval/run_engram.py parses raw context via parse_chunk(). After entity ingestion (needs 512-token chunks for faceted cache hash), rebuild BM25 over individual turns. Raw context = stringified Python list of session chunks.
approach_cards.result: Root-cause fix closing a 35-point gap. 739 chunk-docs → 1282 turn-docs. Became standard config.
approach_cards.notes: CRITICAL BUG (fixed 2026-04-22): ast.literal_eval stripped quotes from Chat Time strings → parse_chunk regex failed → ALL timestamps lost. Fix: pass raw string directly. Timestamps stored separately in store._turn_timestamps, NOT in BM25 text (embedding them dilutes IDF, -4 in exp145).

approach_cards.name: Retrieval component ablation (BM25 / cosine / RRF / rerankers)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Systematically measure each component's Hit@k to find the best stack and isolate whether the bottleneck is ranking or recall.
approach_cards.method: Ablation on 300Q: BM25 alone, cosine (Qwen3-Embed-8B), RRF, then rerankers (mxbai-rerank, Qwen3-Reranker-4B) over RRF top-30.
approach_cards.result: BM25 Hit@5=38.67%, Hit@30=46.00%. Cosine Hit@5=36.67%. RRF Hit@5=40.00%, Hit@30=47.00%. mxbai-rerank Hit@5=42.67%, Hit@10=45.67% — WINNER. Qwen3-Reranker-4B Hit@5=19.00% — DEAD. Ranking SOLVED (97.2% of reachable in top-10). Recall is BOTTLENECK: 159/300 (53%) unreachable by ANY retriever.
approach_cards.notes: Key conclusion repeated across files: ranking is solved, recall is the hard ceiling (extraction/chunking gap, not ranking).

approach_cards.name: Entity prefilter channel
approach_cards.hypothesis: Prefiltering candidates by entity match before BM25 scoring concentrates retrieval on the right region of memory.
approach_cards.method: bm25 + entity_prefilter (entity inverted index), full 5-ctx 300Q. +dynprompt (dynamic prompt) on top.
approach_cards.result: bm25+entity_prefilter: 22.67% SubEM, +6% over plain cosine baseline (16.67%). +dynprompt: 23.00%.
approach_cards.notes: One of the few clearly-additive channels. The entity_index.py regex extractor was the ONLY proven in-pipeline extractor (+6% SubEM).

approach_cards.name: Cross-encoder reranker with entity_prefilter (xenc)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Adding a cross-encoder reranker on top of BM25+entity_prefilter improves precision.
approach_cards.method: bm25 + entity_prefilter + cross-encoder rerank, full 5-ctx 300Q.
approach_cards.result: 17.00% SubEM vs 22.67% without xenc — xenc HURTS by 5.67% WITH entity_prefilter. bm25+xenc clean alone = 17.33% (adds nothing).
approach_cards.notes: Counterintuitive: reranker degrades when entity_prefilter already narrows the pool. Later (2026-04-10) mxbai over RRF DID help — different stack, no entity_prefilter.

approach_cards.name: Chunk-size sweep (cs512 / cs1024 / cs2048)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Larger chunks give the LLM more context (or smaller chunks improve retrieval precision).
approach_cards.method: raw_chunks + entity_prefilter + dynprompt at chunk sizes 512/1024/2048, full 300Q.
approach_cards.result: cs512: 28.00%. cs1024: 26.67% (-1.33%). cs2048: 25.33% (-2.67%). Monotonic regression with size — smaller won.
approach_cards.notes: Bigger context = more LLM distraction. Established cs512 as standard chunk size.

approach_cards.name: Aggregation overflow tuning (aggof20/25/30 + exclusion)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Aggregating an overflow of candidate turns (beyond top-N), optionally excluding already-seen ones, improves multi-turn-aggregation questions.
approach_cards.method: raw_chunks+entpf+dynprompt with aggregation-overflow at 20/25/30, with/without exclusion. Full 300Q.
approach_cards.notes: Per-turn best until structured-query hybrid (31.33%) superseded it 2026-04-07.

approach_cards.name: Structured fact store as additive 3rd RRF channel
approach_cards.hypothesis: An entity-indexed fact store with predicate search, added as an additive 3rd RRF channel (event-calendar 4th for temporal), improves retrieval without replacing BM25.
approach_cards.method: structured_store.py (StructuredFactStore predicate search) + query_parser.py (regex-only question→entity/predicate, no LLM). Scoring subject=5.0/object=4.0/predicate-stem=3.0/substring=2.0, dedup by turn_idx max-score. Populated from SVO cache or live LFM extraction.
approach_cards.result: NEUTRAL — CLOSED. ExpA (Qwen3-30B, 6847 facts) 22.00%; ExpB baseline 22.33%; ExpC (LFM 1.2B, 12619 facts) 23.33% (+1.00%). All within LLM noise. 'Architecture is wrong.'
approach_cards.notes: Qwen3 WORSE than LFM (fewer facts = lower recall — quantity beat quality). Additive, never replaced BM25.

approach_cards.name: Pure structured query as primary retriever (replace BM25)
approach_cards.hypothesis: A structured query over the fact store could serve as the primary retriever, replacing BM25.
approach_cards.method: Run retrieval with pure structured_query as primary instead of BM25 (5-ctx, 300Q).
approach_cards.result: 21.00% SubEM — -7% vs hybrid best. 'Can't replace BM25.'
approach_cards.notes: Confirmed structured query is only viable as a fallback channel, not primary.

approach_cards.name: Hybrid (BM25 baseline + structured-query fallback)
approach_cards.hypothesis: BM25 baseline primary with structured-query fallback captures the best of both without the regression of pure SQ.
approach_cards.method: raw_chunks + entity_prefilter + dynprompt baseline with structured-query fallback merge. 5-ctx, 300Q, gpt-4o-mini.
approach_cards.result: 31.33% SubEM — best as of 2026-04-07 (up from 28.67% aggof25 baseline).
approach_cards.notes: All add-ons DEAD: +exact_words_prompt 30.00%, +set_union_merge 30.33%, +both 28.33%, +noun_chunk 31.67% (noise +4/-3).

approach_cards.name: Temporal inference engine (_infer_temporal_diff)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Many failures are date-arithmetic ('how many days ago'); deterministically BM25-searching event dates, looking up stored timestamps, and computing diffs rescues temporal questions the LLM gets wrong.
approach_cards.method: _infer_temporal_diff: BM25 event search → timestamp lookup from _turn_timestamps (doc_id→ISO) → date-diff. _add_time_units generates days, inclusive days, plain numbers, exact/approximate weeks (±2 days of N*7).
approach_cards.result: ctx0 reached 80.00% (48/60) at exp146b. Rescued qi=7 (+1). Contributed +11 over the gold-in-conversation ceiling.
approach_cards.notes: Timestamps stored separately (exp145c) — embedding in BM25 diluted IDF (exp145 -4). Later REMOVED in honest-baseline cleanup as hard-coded computation.

approach_cards.name: Evidence-numbers gate widening (exp151)
approach_cards.hypothesis: _add_evidence_numbers checked only line 1 for digits, but _add_number_equivalents writes the digit equivalent on line 2, so valid answers were missed; checking the first two lines rescues them.
approach_cards.method: Widen _add_evidence_numbers gate to check first TWO lines for digits instead of only the first.
approach_cards.result: 5-ctx SubEM 65.00% (195/300), up from exp146b 191/300 (+4). ctx1 +2, ctx4 +2. Per-ctx: ctx0 48, ctx1 40, ctx2 37, ctx3 32, ctx4 38 of 60.
approach_cards.notes: We exceed gold-in-conversation ceiling via temporal inference (+11), synthetic computation (19), inclusive-day format, de-gated rescue, this gate fix.

approach_cards.name: Exhausted retrieval/format/temporal micro-experiments (exp147-155)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Incremental tweaks (number-word formats, half-weeks, inclusive-day variants, temporal verb boosts, hybrid temporal RRF, evidence perspective shift/reversal/truncation) could squeeze more SubEM.
approach_cards.method: Systematic ablations: exp147 number-word/half-weeks; exp148 inclusive-day; exp149 verb boost+top_k30; exp150 hybrid BM25+cosine temporal RRF; exp152 your→my perspective; exp154 reversed evidence; exp155 truncated evidence (3000 chars).
approach_cards.result: All neutral or regressed. exp147/148: 0 rescues. exp149: -2 (broad verbs HURT). exp150: -3 (cosine dilutes BM25 precision). exp152: net 0. exp154: -3 ctx0. exp155: -3 ctx0.
approach_cards.notes: Gold format coverage COMPLETE — failures are wrong NUMBERS not FORMAT. Temporal event search: BM25-only top_k=15 optimal; cosine/wider/verb-boost all HURT. LLM needs full best-first evidence.

approach_cards.name: EventFrame architecture (topic-shift segmentation + temporal contiguity)
approach_cards.hypothesis: The system is 100% content-addressable and missing an index layer that BINDS fragments into episodes; EventFrames (turns bound with timestamp/gist/entities/prev-next) plus frame-aware contiguity (retrieve N → also pull N±1) address the binding problem.
approach_cards.method: EventFrame dataclass + EventFrameIndex in foundry/storage.py. Topic-shift segmentation via entity overlap between consecutive turns (not fixed-size). Frame-aware contiguity in recall() via use_event_frames. 47 tests.
approach_cards.result: 196/300 SubEM (65.33%) — matches baseline EXACTLY, no regression and no gain. All 47 tests + 5 contract assertions pass.
approach_cards.notes: Inspired by EM-LLM (contiguity buffer) and SEEM (event frames). Architecturally correct for episodic recall but didn't move SubEM.

approach_cards.name: Content-addressable vs index-based memory framing
approach_cards.hypothesis: All retrievers (BM25, cosine, reranker, entity, Hopfield/Triadic/SDM) are content-addressable; the problem is BINDING not retrieval — need an index-based layer (hippocampal index / provenance pointers / event frames).
approach_cards.method: Conceptual analysis classifying every retrieval method as content-addressable vs index-based; rank missing capabilities by impact.
approach_cards.result: Framing adopted as guiding principle. Ranked missing: (1) temporal contiguity, (2) event-level gists, (3) provenance pointers, (4) surprise-based segmentation. 'Our system is 100% content-addressable.'
approach_cards.notes: Produced EventFrames (neutral) and motivated 'search obs, serve turns'. Explains why content-addressable tweaks plateaued: LME needs reasoning/binding, not better closest-match.

approach_cards.name: Foundry greenfield build (BM25-primary + 3-tier routing, spec-driven)
approach_cards.hypothesis: A from-scratch, spec-driven universal memory system with BM25 primary, deterministic routing, and computation engines elevated to co-primary closes the gap retrieval-only couldn't. The bottleneck is COMPUTATION, not retrieval.
approach_cards.method: TDD-migration greenfield: Phase 1 spec (4918+ lines), Phase 2 tests (587 tests, 31 files, all failing ImportError), Phase 3 adversarial (4 passes, 112 findings, 13 FATAL mitigated), Phase 3.25 discriminative (9-agent tribunal, 76+ tests), Phase 3.5 prior art (47 projects).
approach_cards.result: H1 (BM25 primary) VALIDATED WITH QUALIFICATION — retrieval NOT the bottleneck, 53% need computation. H2 (deterministic routing) PARTIAL — 80% deterministic / 20% LLM. H3 (entity resolution substring+embedding) FALSIFIED — 100% false merge at scale. Build loop (Phase 5) still TODO 2026-04-14.
approach_cards.notes: Convergent insight: bottleneck is COMPUTATION not retrieval. EntityStore BM25 replaces substring+embedding; EntitySplitter for false-merge recovery.

approach_cards.name: Agentic ReAct retrieval (AgenticRetriever, 7 tools)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Single-pass retrieval is wrong — humans search iteratively; an agent with a 7-tool toolbox searching iteratively beats single similarity search.
approach_cards.method: ReAct agent (gpt-4o-mini), 7 tools (search_memory/entities/related/temporal, read_turn, answer, execute_python) wired to BM25+cosine RRF, cross-encoder, Allen engine (1404 events), 3-layer entity graph, sandboxed date arithmetic. 34 discriminative tests pass.
approach_cards.result: POC 38.3% SubEM on 60q BM25-only vs 28.67% prev single-pass. BUT later verdict: agent HURTS for LME, -5 SubEM vs deterministic recall(). Declared DEAD for LME.
approach_cards.notes: FAISS segfault fix: import SentenceTransformer before faiss on macOS ARM64. Intended as trace-generation stage for distillation; deterministic recall() won.

approach_cards.name: Traces → Deterministic → Distilled SLM pipeline (4-phase)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Capture agentic traces, extract per-question-type patterns, hardcode common patterns as deterministic pipelines (no query-time LLM), and fine-tune a 0.6-1.4B SLM for tool-routing on novel cases.
approach_cards.method: Phase 1 agentic capture (DONE). Phase 2 pattern extraction, Phase 3 deterministic pipelines (regex/tiny classifier <1ms → hardcoded <10ms), Phase 4 distilled SLM tool-loop (~50ms/step).
approach_cards.result: Phase 1 complete; Phases 2-4 left as TODO. Superseded once deterministic recall() beat the agent by 5 SubEM, making the premise moot.
approach_cards.notes: Tied to Hebbian bridge idea (frequent paths → parametric, unused decay). Never reached production.

approach_cards.name: Oracle-as-code-generator (code oracle, no LLM arithmetic)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Never let the LLM do arithmetic; classify question → if arithmetic/temporal/counting, have a small model generate Python → exec() → deterministic answer.
approach_cards.method: code_oracle.py: classify → build facts prompt from evidence → SLM generates Python → safe exec() (blocks os/sys/subprocess, 5s SIGALRM). CLI --code_oracle --code_oracle_model. Additive alongside regex post-processing.
approach_cards.result: 5-Q micro: llama-3.2-3b 5/5, liquid 1.2B 4/5 (vs 2-3/5 in-head). 5-ctx LME +2 (61.00%, 183/300). LME-500: DEAD — 0 improvements, 2 regressions (-2 net).
approach_cards.notes: Code-gen > scene reconstruction > raw answering. Dead on LME-500: SLM can't generate useful code from noisy 500-turn evidence.

approach_cards.name: Dual-tier scoring (SubEM || noise-aware LLM judge)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Long preference-paragraph gold answers are unscorable by SubEM, but a noise-aware LLM judge (ignore extraneous text, check if correct answer appears anywhere) rescues them as a second tier.
approach_cards.method: Score with SubEM OR noise-aware judge prompt. Tested gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4o, hybrid, and union judges on exp151 output.
approach_cards.result: SubEM||noise-aware-mini: 76.0% (228/300), +33 rescues (13 pref, 20 factual) — NEW BEST COMBINED. Combined mini||4o: 76.7% (230/300), +35. Standalone: noise-aware mini 58.3% (175/300), 4o 60.7% (182/300), standard mini 55.3% (166/300).
approach_cards.notes: 30 preference Qs permanently SubEM=0; judge rescues 13-15/30. single-session-assistant category 100% solved.

approach_cards.name: MABench monolithic winner (cooc+triadic+decompose+CR+bm25_hops)
approach_cards.hypothesis: On FactConsolidation-MH, combining co-occurrence boost, triadic memory, query decomposition, per-hop conflict resolution, and BM25-hops yields strong multi-hop SubEM.
approach_cards.method: Monolithic hermes_agent: --cooc_boost --triadic --decompose_query --conflict_resolution --cr_per_hop --bm25_hops --chunk_size 512, mh_262k, gpt-4o-mini.
approach_cards.result: SubEM 39 (best 2026-03-25), 35 on rerun (±4 LLM variance). cooc-only baseline 20-22. Ceiling 98 (2 unsolvable). 61 failures: entity_confusion 60 (98%), llm_format 1.
approach_cards.notes: Multi-hop cascade ~70%/hop → 0.7^4=24% for 4-hop. NOT retrieval — all failures had full context; it's LLM selection. FC paper SOTA arXiv 2507.05257.

approach_cards.name: Composed agent refactor (vs monolithic)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Refactoring monolithic hermes_agent into composed agent.py preserves accuracy (no regression).
approach_cards.method: Re-run winner config under composed agent vs monolithic (BM25 fix applied), mh_262k, gpt-4o-mini.
approach_cards.result: Composed 33 vs monolithic rerun 35 (same day) — 2 points, within ±4. No regression. Per-query: 24 shared, 9 composed-only, 8 mono-only.
approach_cards.notes: Validated composed agent (now the only agent; monolithic deprecated) is equivalent. cooc+bm25-only monolithic = 32.

approach_cards.name: FC feature stack ported to LME (cooc+cr+bm25h+tri+xenc)
approach_cards.hypothesis: The feature stack that won on FactConsolidation-MH should transfer to LongMemEval.
approach_cards.method: Apply full MABench winner feature stack to LME, full 5-ctx 300Q.
approach_cards.result: 2.67% SubEM — 'FC features catastrophic on LME.' Far below plain cosine (16.67%).
approach_cards.notes: Strong negative transfer — FC (Wikidata counterfactual KG) features actively harm LME (real-conversation memory). Different benchmark = different optimum. Includes the triadic feature that helped on FC.

approach_cards.name: REBEL knowledge-graph triple extraction
approach_cards.hypothesis: REBEL (seq2seq RE trained on Wikipedia→Wikidata, F1=93 NYT) builds a high-quality KG boosting SubEM — especially as MABench is Wikidata-derived.
approach_cards.method: Enable --rebel_kg on MABench winner; parse REBEL output into KG triples.
approach_cards.result: SubEM 29 with REBEL vs 39 without — costs 10 points. seq2seq GENERATES text → hallucinates property labels. Parser bug swaps relation/object. Kept DISABLED.
approach_cards.notes: Benchmark-advantaged yet STILL hurt 10 points — generative-RE hallucination outweighs the advantage. Rejected in favor of extractive (ReLiK) / NER-derived edges.

approach_cards.name: Conflict-resolution detection matrix (NLI + cosine)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Detecting fact conflicts (for supersession) is best done by combining cosine similarity and NLI entailment rather than either alone.
approach_cards.method: Grid over cosine thresholds × NLI on candidate fact pairs. NLI = DeBERTa-v3-xsmall (22M params, CPU). Measure F1.
approach_cards.result: Best F1: cos>0.50 AND NLI = 79% F1.
approach_cards.notes: Used for per-hop conflict resolution in the MABench winner.

approach_cards.name: FactConsolidation-MH ground-truth bug discovery + serial patch
approach_cards.hypothesis: Low FC-MH ceiling is benchmark error: MQUAKE pools all questions' edits into one shared fact pool, so per-question expected answers are stale (cross-question counterfactual interference).
approach_cards.method: Audit all 100 questions against the pooled fact set (18,332 facts). Classify broken answers; serial-swap patch (majority-wins) to make answers self-consistent.
approach_cards.result: 34/100 have wrong ground truth (19 INTERMEDIATE_REDIRECT, 15 FINAL_HOP_SUPERSEDED, 1 DEAD_END). 46 serial swaps fix 93/100; 6 IRRECONCILABLE.
approach_cards.notes: Benchmark itself broken for 34% — explains a chunk of the FC ceiling. Reinforces 'benchmark is diagnostic, not target.'

approach_cards.name: Bottom-up KG Query Engine (14 ops, 3 tiers)
approach_cards.hypothesis: The hard part of KG memory is the OPERATIONS (predicate-vocab mismatch, entity resolution, numeric extraction), not DSL plumbing. A Universal Fact schema + 14 typed ops built bottom-up against real LME covers 82% of questions.
approach_cards.method: Universal Fact dataclass + EntityFactStore (predicate/temporal indices, fuzzy_match). 14 ops in 3 tiers: Tier1 (LOOKUP/COUNT/SUM/LIST/COMPARE/TEMPORAL_LOOKUP/ORDER/DIFF/TRAVERSE/SUPERSEDE), Tier2 (KNN/RECOMMEND), Tier3 (ENTITY/COMMUNITY_SUMMARY). Each op = tested class benchmarked per-op.
approach_cards.result: Planning/baseline. KG-resolvable 245/300 (82%); current 48/245 (~20% SubEM); ceiling ~200/245 (82%). Per-op: LOOKUP 66Q 18%→80%, COUNT 64Q 27%→70%, TEMPORAL_DIFF 36Q 8%→50%, TEMPORAL_LOOKUP 31Q 19%→60%, SUM 20Q 10%→60%, ORDER 19Q 26%→70%. PREFERENCE 30Q 0% (needs judge), RECALL_VERBATIM 25Q 8%.
approach_cards.notes: Oracle survey: Zep/Graphiti (94.8% DMR bi-temporal Neo4j), MS GraphRAG, LlamaIndex NL2Cypher, HydraRAG. NONE handle counting/aggregation over personal conversational data. Decision: build custom.

approach_cards.name: KnowledgeGraph module (rustworkx PPR traversal)
approach_cards.hypothesis: None of 9 existing structures give a traversable relational graph. A rustworkx PyDiGraph queried via Personalized PageRank (HippoRAG) compresses multi-hop reasoning into one computation; node-specificity weighting (1/num_facts) up-weights rare entities.
approach_cards.method: rustworkx PyDiGraph, bidirectional edges from triples. PPR at query time with personalization vector. Node weight=1/num_facts_mentioning. Supersession removes old/adds new/prunes orphans. One channel in layered per-hop fallback. mabench/knowledge_graph.py.
approach_cards.result: TDD module (29 KG tests). rustworkx 0.17.1, PPR ~10ms/100K edges, 3-100x faster than NetworkX. No end-to-end SubEM. Critical bottleneck: triple-extraction coverage (~45 unique S,P keys).
approach_cards.notes: PPR decays 0.85^4=0.52 for 4-hop → drowns in dense graphs. KEEP decompose, AUGMENT each hop graph-aware rather than replace. BFS rejected (exponential blowup).

approach_cards.name: HyperedgeIntersection (intermediate-entity soft penalty)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Multi-hop retrieval can be guided by softly penalizing (0.1x, not hard filter) facts not mentioning the INTERMEDIATE answer entity from the previous hop, avoiding the precision collapse of hard filtering.
approach_cards.method: Entity-constrained per-hop retrieval reusing GLiNER entity index. After hop N returns entity X, penalize facts NOT mentioning X for hop N+1 by 0.1x. mabench/hyperedge_intersection.py.
approach_cards.result: In progress (tests underway). Explicitly references prior SubEM=9 hard-filter catastrophe motivating the 0.1x soft penalty. No standalone SubEM.
approach_cards.notes: Layer in per-hop fallback: (0) triple_index ~0ms, (1) PPR ~10ms, (2) entity intersection ~1ms, (3) cosine+BM25+triadic ~100ms.

approach_cards.name: Hard entity-first filtering (multi-hop)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Hard-filter retrieval to facts mentioning the query entity to constrain multi-hop search.
approach_cards.method: Hard filter on entity membership during multi-hop retrieval (predecessor to HyperedgeIntersection).
approach_cards.result: SubEM=9 catastrophe — hard filter collapsed retrieval. Motivated the 0.1x soft penalty and intermediate-entity formulation.
approach_cards.notes: Hard filters destroy recall when extraction coverage is sparse.

approach_cards.name: spaCy / OpenIE dependency-parse triple extraction
approach_cards.hypothesis: Dependency-parse SVO patterns extract relational triples cheaply with no model.
approach_cards.method: spaCy dep-parse SVO (nsubj→VERB→dobj/attr/pobj), single tokens. OpenIE as alternative.
approach_cards.result: ~45 unique (S,P) keys from 18K facts — 'essentially empty', too few for graph density. English-only, not cross-lingual. OpenIE gave 13K edges (too noisy).
approach_cards.notes: The ~45-key sparsity is the recurring 'empty KG' bottleneck. Must be replaced by cross-lingual RE (ReLiK) for universal memory.

approach_cards.name: Split-flow triple extraction (primitive for supersession, rich for graph)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Supersession wants FEW conservative triples; graph hops want MANY rich triples. Feeding the rich extractor into supersession poisons it — splitting the flows keeps supersession safe while adding coverage.
approach_cards.method: Two extractors. Primitive (Segmenter._extract_triples): single-token SVO → few. Rich (_extract_acl_triples): copular/acl/compound/prep/passive/multi-word → many. Supersession iterates primitive only; triple_index = primitive ∪ rich; graph hops read compound keys.
approach_cards.result: Unified rich extractor: SubEM 39→36 (REGRESSION — supersession over-fires on broad keys like (X,be)). Split: supersession unchanged, graph hops additive (no regression).
approach_cards.notes: Key lesson: DO NOT make Segmenter use _extract_acl_triples — broad keys make supersession fire too aggressively.

approach_cards.name: GLiNER2 unified NER+RE extractor
approach_cards.hypothesis: GLiNER2 (fastino/gliner2-base-v1, 205M, DeBERTa-v3) extracts dense relational triples per-fact without an LLM, orders-of-magnitude denser than spaCy.
approach_cards.method: GLiNER2Extractor (composition, config-gated, lazy load, pickle-safe). 28 default relation types, threshold 0.5, self-referential filter. mabench/gliner2_extractor.py.
approach_cards.result: ~2.1 triples/fact → ~37K triples from 18K facts (vs spaCy 45 keys). 23 tests pass. BUT too slow: 117ms/fact batch CPU (~35min/18K facts); full uni-encoder 97s/chunk for 64 facts with 28 types; load 57s.
approach_cards.notes: The 97s/chunk latency triggered the split NER/RE architecture. Threshold 0.5 sweet spot.

approach_cards.name: GLiNER2 latency diagnosis → split NER/RE (bi-edge NER + ReLiK RE)
approach_cards.hypothesis: GLiNER2 latency scales near-quadratically with relation-label count (labels concatenated with text in uni-encoder); a fast NER-edge path serves KG+triadic while only supersession pays for slow RE.
approach_cards.method: Diagnose latency vs label count. Fast path: gliner-bi-edge-v2.0 NER-only, pre-encode labels once (encode_labels), co-occurrence edges by pairing entities within a fact. Slow path: ReLiK (relik-relation-extraction-nyt-large) for (S,P,O), supersession only.
approach_cards.result: Near-quadratic: 3 types 8.8s / 7 12.4s / 14 28.3s / 28 58-97s. Fast bi-edge 0.008s/text (bs=128), encode_labels 2.4s once. Co-occurrence = 10-50x more edges than explicit RE (solves empty-KG). ReLiK NOT YET BENCHMARKED.
approach_cards.notes: Bi-encoder RE does NOT exist in GLiNER ecosystem as of 2026-03-27. ReLiK (ACL2024) F1=95 NYT, 40x fastest; GLiREL (NAACL2025) F1=74 zero-shot.

approach_cards.name: Free-form / ad-hoc triple extraction (unbounded ontology)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Let the LLM emit triples with whatever predicates/types it wants; coverage will be high.
approach_cards.method: Multipass/property-triple extraction with no fixed schema, arbitrary entity types and predicates.
approach_cards.result: FAILS: 190 ad-hoc entity types, predicate fragmentation, 1.7% SubEM on 54K triples. Unbounded vocab makes facts unretrievable (query predicate never matches extraction predicate).
approach_cards.notes: Motivating failure for bounded ontology. Production confirms bounded: Know Ontology (5 types), Zep (3+custom), Memoria (87.1%).

approach_cards.name: 28 universal relation types + plain (S,P,O) schema
approach_cards.hypothesis: 28 relation types (7 categories) is the sweet spot — GLiREL caps at ~25 labels/instance, top 15-20 types cover 80%+ (Zipf). Plain (S,P,O) in rustworkx beats RDF (reification=4-triple overhead; SPARQL/OWL would break supersession).
approach_cards.method: 28 core types across Taxonomic/Mereological/Spatial-Temporal/Causal/Agentive/Descriptive/Epistemic. Two-tier: Tier1 28 frozen universal (supersession), Tier2 domain-prefixed (med:treats). Plain property graph, no RDF/URIs/OWL.
approach_cards.result: Validated by oracle survey of 15+ schemas (ConceptNet, Schema.org, Wikidata, YAGO, DBpedia, SUMO, Cyc) — every chosen relation appears in 3+. 28 chosen empirically (GLiREL cap + supersession needs born_in/works_in/located_in distinguishable).
approach_cards.notes: RDF explicitly rejected. Later superseded by the 9-facet shape-based ontology (2026-04-12).

approach_cards.name: 10-type bounded ontology
approach_cards.hypothesis: A fixed ~10-type ontology (Person/Place/Event/Activity/Thing/Preference/Project/Skill/Organization/Metric) with typed slots fixes the predicate-fragmentation failure of free-form.
approach_cards.method: 10 named types with typed slots, modeled on Know Ontology/Zep/Memoria. disc_typed_svo.py (LFM 1.2B structured JSON) closest in-pipeline.
approach_cards.result: Proposed; motivated by free-form failure (1.7%). Cache audit: qa_triples 60% entities/93% triples grounded; user_turn_triples 8.3% SubEM. Superseded days later by 9-facet schema rather than fully adopted.
approach_cards.notes: 6 extraction systems inventoried; entity_index.py regex was the ONLY proven in-pipeline (+6% SubEM).

approach_cards.name: 9-facet shape-based (faceted) ontology
approach_cards.hypothesis: Define entities by SHAPE (which facets are populated) not named types. 9 universal facets (what/who/when/where/quantity/frequency/how/sentiment/status) generalize across domains/languages, avoiding predicate fragmentation.
approach_cards.method: 9 facets, facet_name as predicate. Two-phase graph build: (1) pre-register all entity names in alias_index (prevent false substring merges), (2) ingest facets as triples. Grounding verification: fact.object must appear in fact.source_text. mabench/ontology.py.
approach_cards.result: IMPLEMENTED. 308 tests (test_ontology + test_entity_graph). Grounding check catches model-inference injections ('Delta→airline' fails because 'airline' not in 'I fly Delta'). Graph = user's words, not model's interpretation.
approach_cards.notes: Doctors live in 'who' facet not 'what'. Became the validated ontology direction (winning unified-pool type hierarchy in later work).

approach_cards.name: Layered EntityGraph (STATED / INFERRED / DERIVED)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Three EntityGraph instances sharing names but different facts let the system add semantic bridges and computed patterns WITHOUT model inference corrupting the user's literal facts; answers come only from STATED.
approach_cards.method: STATED (user words + grounding, permanent), INFERRED (semantic bridges, rebuildable cache), DERIVED (computed gist patterns, recomputable). Separate instances. Gist extraction no-LLM: convergent (groupby facet), progression (deltas), co-occurrence (mention_turns intersection).
approach_cards.result: Adversarially validated: inferred can't overwrite stated; hallucinated entities don't leak; wipe+rebuild leaves stated intact. BUT NET NEUTRAL for LME SubEM — multipass triples too noisy; needs clean faceted extraction to pay off.
approach_cards.notes: Model comparison: Gemma 3 4B best (76%/18%hall/62%/2.3s); Qwen3.5 9B (76%/19%/62%/5.0s); LFM 2.5 1.2B (86%/62%hall/33%/1.4s — too much hallucination).

approach_cards.name: Passive consolidation — unified type hierarchy (librarian/card-catalog)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Building ONE entity type tree at ingestion (mention bridges + TF-IDF specificity + co-occurrence subsumption) lets a single tree answer count/sum/when by walking it and doing different math at leaves.
approach_cards.method: Three cards/mention (name/what/who) linked by a 'mention bridge'. TF-IDF over labels ranks specificity. Co-occurrence subsumption: chunks(specific)⊆chunks(general) at 70% → general is parent. Unified pool = entity names + who + what.
approach_cards.result: Unified pool is the WINNING type-hierarchy method: 15/20 (remaining 5 = extraction gaps, not hierarchy errors).
approach_cards.notes: Doctors in 'who' facet not 'what' — index both. One tree, three questions: count (count names), sum (sum quantity facet), when (sort by when facet).

approach_cards.name: QA-driven (5W1H) triple extraction
approach_cards.hypothesis: LLMs are better at Q&A than at generating arbitrary triple schemas. Do text→5W1H QA pairs→triples instead of text→triples→normalize; QA framing yields natural specific predicates.
approach_cards.method: Call 1: generate WHO/WHAT/WHEN/WHERE/HOW_MANY/HOW QA pairs (confirmed facts, atomic 1-5 word answers, subject='user' for self). Call 2: QA→triples. Planned DySECT feedback loop (top-K predicates as few-shot → converge).
approach_cards.result: Llama 3.1 8B FP16 = 8/8 perfect (2-6 facts/turn); Llama 3.1 8B q4_k_m = 8/8 perfect/cleaner (sweet spot); LFM 2.5 1.2B = 8/8 correct but noisy. Predicates: weekly_work_hours, age, number_of_bikes, undergrad_institution.
approach_cards.notes: qa_triples cache (3704) had highest grounding 60%/93%. Sources: SocraticKG, DySECT, Distill-SynthKG, PROM, LangMem.

approach_cards.name: Rich extractor (textacy + custom patterns)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Augmenting textacy SVO with hand-written patterns (copular, verb+prep, possessive, numeric) raises triple coverage on hard sentence forms.
approach_cards.method: mabench/rich_extractor.py. textacy SVO (conjuncts, xcomp, compound nouns) + copular + verb+prep + possessive + numeric patterns.
approach_cards.result: Coverage 8/8 test sentences (was 4/8 with basic SVO). Precompute: 87,623 raw → 43,096 normalized triples.
approach_cards.notes: Caches: perturn_rich_cache_cs512 (43K), perturn_spacy_cache_cs512 (34K basic SVO).

approach_cards.name: LFM2.5-1.2B SVO entity extraction (V4 prompt)
approach_cards.hypothesis: A tiny 1.2B model (LFM2.5) with a 'thorough and exhaustive' SVO prompt and json_schema output extracts dense entities cheaply, beating a 30B model on entity-indexing metrics for LME.
approach_cards.method: liquid/lfm2.5-1.2b via LM Studio, SVO with mandatory json_schema. V4 prompt: extract every entity/number/date/feature; subject must be specific named entity (never I/you/user); extract every list item; subjects 1-3 words.
approach_cards.result: 27 LME turns: 289 facts, 88 unique entities, 13.8% user subjects, 0 parse errors, 1.79s/turn, 23.8% reachability. Beats Qwen3-30B on ALL entity-indexing metrics (Qwen3: 74 entities, 3 errors, 3.34s/turn, 19.0%). BUT on FC: Qwen3 100% clean vs LFM 92% → NOT for FC.
approach_cards.notes: LFM rules: NEVER few-shot (catastrophic contamination); ALWAYS json_schema (0% parse without); multi-pass DOES NOT WORK (pass 2 = 0 new). Keep Qwen3 for FC, LFM for LME entity indexing.

approach_cards.name: Failed SVO/typing/alias pre-experiments
approach_cards.hypothesis: Typed SVO extraction, SVO entity supplementation into the inverted index, and alias resolution (query-time or ingestion-time) improve entity-based recall.
approach_cards.method: (1) LFM 1.2B typed SVO; (2) SVO entity supplementation into entity_inv_idx; (3) query-time alias resolution; (4) ingestion-time flat alias dict.
approach_cards.result: (1) 1972 unnormalized types, 55% hit@10 — WORSE than baseline. (2) 22.33% SubEM — regression. (3) chicken-and-egg, 0 new wins. (4) collision explosion, too noisy.
approach_cards.notes: Documented as 'what failed before (don't repeat)'. All four entity-normalization/aliasing strategies failed before structured-store work.

approach_cards.name: Residual-stream entity-position retrieval (KV-Direct gate)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Per arXiv:2603.19664, the residual stream is the sole Markov state (KV redundant, 7-27x compression); entity-position residuals serve as identity-preserving embeddings enabling an entity-cosine gate that penalizes wrong-entity matches and gives a safe dream-merge criterion.
approach_cards.method: 3 iterations. v1 SmolLM2-135M last-token (flawed). v2 Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B entity-position residuals. v3 definitive: in-context vs ISOLATED entity residuals. Multiplicative gate: cos>0.95→1.0, 0.80-0.95→0.5, <0.80→0.2; final=cosine*gate.
approach_cards.result: v2 AUC=1.000 but only fact-to-fact (misleading). v3 France-vs-Germany cos/self/gap: Layer-14 in-context 0.992/0.806/0.006 (USELESS — template bleeds); raw token embeddings 0.585/1.000/0.415 (best gap, no semantics); ISOLATED entity layer-14 0.866/1.000/0.134 (WINNER). Effective rank 56/1024 (5.5%), lower than paper's 27-33%.
approach_cards.notes: Discrimination test only — NO end-to-end SubEM. Linear blend (α=0.3) changes nothing; multiplicative gate needed. Untested: end-to-end SubEM, hardest confusers, ingestion cost.

approach_cards.name: Triadic Memory (3D SDR tensor) — prior-art study
approach_cards.hypothesis: A 3D binary tensor for SDR triple association (capacity (N/P)³, one-shot perfect retrieval) could serve as the binding structure for episodic memory.
approach_cards.method: Studied research/TriadicMemory/. Sparse distributed representation triple store.
approach_cards.result: DEAD END — operates on SDRs not embeddings, still content-addressable, no temporal binding. Wrong abstraction for LME (needs reasoning over facts).
approach_cards.notes: Echoes NLCDM/Hopfield finding: content-addressable is wrong abstraction. Triadic was also a feature in the MABench winner (--triadic) where it helped on FC, but the LME port scored 2.67%.

approach_cards.name: EM-LLM / REMem / SEEM prior-art studies
approach_cards.hypothesis: External episodic-memory systems (surprise segmentation, hybrid memory graphs, two-layer hierarchy + provenance) could inform our episodic index layer.
approach_cards.method: EM-LLM: surprise-based segmentation (perplexity>γσ+μ), attention-graph refinement, 30% budget for block±1 neighbors. REMem: 4-node-type graph (verbatim/gists/facts/entities), 3 extraction passes, 5-tool ReAct (max 3 steps). SEEM (arXiv:2601.06411, no code): two-layer + Reverse Provenance Expansion.
approach_cards.result: EM-LLM published LongBench 51.58 (their RAG 36.44, FC 39.30), 100% passkey @10M tokens. REMem published 55.2% but GPT-4o judge NOT SubEM — 'our 66% SubEM genuinely ahead.' SEEM no reproduction. Adopted: temporal contiguity, gists-as-separate-modality, provenance pointers (#3 ranked missing capability).
approach_cards.notes: Confirms our metric stricter than competitors'. Validates gists-as-separate-modality over text augmentation (augmentation HURTS, exp145). SEEM RPE motivated 'search obs, serve turns' provenance resolution. Studied as prior art, not run on our pipeline.

approach_cards.name: Hebbian bridge (searchable → parametric, decay)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Frequently-fired retrieval paths should strengthen (cache hits → eventually parametric/instant), unused paths decay — Hebbian learning applied to memory, with supersession/decay handling changing facts.
approach_cards.method: Conceptual design in the two-tier model: searchable (non-parametric) memory with a bridge to parametric (weights) via repetition, conflict resolution at search level, analogous overwrite at parametric level.
approach_cards.result: Design-stage only; no quantitative result. (Parametric/CL experiments — TTT, LoRA SFT — tracked elsewhere as dead-ends in MEMORY.md.)
approach_cards.notes: Human-memory analogy: parametric=childhood/personality (imperfect but instant), searchable=notes (perfect but effortful), bridge=spaced repetition.

approach_cards.name: Allen ORB Temporal Engine (hybrid BM25+Qwen3-8B)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Encoding extracted events as time intervals and using Allen's 13 interval relations as deterministic retrieval/reasoning primitives answers ordering/duration/contains questions without asking the LLM to reason over raw text.
approach_cards.method: mabench/allen_engine.py: 13 Allen relations + 5 convenience methods (ordering, distance, duration_between, duration_of, contains). Hybrid retrieval = BM25 + Qwen3-Embedding-8B (4096-dim) cosine fused via RRF (k=60), entity filter, SVO-aware 3-level matching. Gemma-3-4b for question analysis. Precomputed 42913 events from gpt-4o-mini.
approach_cards.result: 21/30 (70%) on Allen-addressable temporal questions; 22/30 (73.3%) counting unit-format match. By op: ordering 78%, duration_between 80%, contains 67%, distance 50%.
approach_cards.notes: Only 30/75 temporal instances are Allen-addressable; counting=18, fact_recall=5, age=3, preference/schedule=19 should NOT route through Allen. 9 failures: wrong-event=5, entity-fail=1, extraction-date-error=1, unit-format=1, not-temporal=1. RunPod: sentence_transformers broken, used raw transformers.

approach_cards.name: Always-on Temporal Pipeline (3 pieces: Chat Time ingest + proximity rerank + code-computed deltas)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Chat Time markers give ~1-day-resolution timestamps for free; threading them through every fact (ingest), proximity-weighting retrieval, and code-computing date deltas (LLM only formats) provides temporal grounding with no LLM extraction and runs unconditionally (neutral when absent), cooc_boost-style.
approach_cards.method: P1: temporal.py regex (compact+spaced Chat Time), MemoryEntry.session_time field, inheritance via _last_session_time in store.py. P2: temporal_proximity=1/(1+alpha*days_apart), alpha=0.01, in _apply_temporal_proximity() after role weighting, returns 1.0 when dates absent, CLI --temporal_alpha. P3: query_pipeline.py enrich_with_temporal()/format_temporal_context(), code computes abs(date_a-date_b).days, injects '[2023-01-15, 10 days before query]' + pairwise deltas.
approach_cards.result: P1: 19/19 ingestion tests, 14/16 dateparser (2 expected fails: 'early January','last March'). P2+P3: 30 pipeline tests passing (parsing/proximity/enrichment/formatting/E2E). No standalone SubEM delta recorded.
approach_cards.notes: No-conditional-branches always-on design. Chose session_time (Chat Time) over event_time (~1-day free vs dateparser+LLM). Entity registry cap (max_entries=50) prevents unbounded prompt injection. LME temporal-reasoning=25% of queries (75 Qs): 'days ago'=28%, 'which first'=29%, 'days between'=24%.

approach_cards.name: ADELIE-SFT-3B + v3_simple extraction prompt
approach_cards.hypothesis: A small IE-fine-tuned 3B model (ADELIE-SFT-3B = Llama-3.2-3B) with the simplest event+date prompt extracts event/date pairs universally (no regex exploit), if the chat timestamp is supplied.
approach_cards.method: Prompt v3_simple: 'What events happened and when?... Message date: {chat_date}. Return JSON [{event,when,date}]'. Manual Tulu chat template (tokenizer template is None). JSON regex r'(\[\{.*\}?\])'. DSPy-style prompt_tuning.py, 6 variants.
approach_cards.result: 100.0% (8/8) on 3B. Beat v4_fewshot 87.5%, v5_ner_events 87.5%, v6_structured 87.5%, v2_event_date 75%, v1_ace 0%.
approach_cards.notes: Chat timestamp in prompt is ESSENTIAL: 0%→100%. Simpler prompts win on 3B. ACE-ontology prompts (triggers, not event+date) are wrong for this task. First principle: regex date extraction is a benchmark exploit; production must use LLM.

approach_cards.name: ADELIE-SFT-1.5B extraction (Qwen2.5-1.5B)
approach_cards.hypothesis: A smaller 1.5B IE model would be cheaper if it could match the 3B on event/date extraction.
approach_cards.method: Same DSPy-style harness, 6 prompt variants, on ADELIE-SFT-1.5B (Qwen2.5-1.5B), same 8-item set.
approach_cards.result: DEAD. Best v4_fewshot 37.5% (3/8); v5/v6 37.5%; v1_ace 12.5%; v3_simple 0%.
approach_cards.notes: 1.5B hallucinates JS code with v3_simple, can't follow structured JSON. The prompt that maxed the 3B was the worst on 1.5B — capacity floor, not a prompt problem.

approach_cards.name: Regex date-extraction ceiling (Ablation 08)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Measure the upper bound of temporal info recoverable via pure regex + Chat Time, to prove the information is present even though regex is not the production path.
approach_cards.method: ablation_testing/08_temporal_calendar.py: extract_content_dates() (regex + dateparser for today/yesterday) + chat timestamps, coverage over temporal questions.
approach_cards.result: 40/41 (97.6%) content-date coverage.
approach_cards.notes: Explicitly a ceiling/diagnostic, NOT production — 'regex date extraction is a benchmark exploit.' Proves the INFORMATION IS THERE; production must extract via LLM. dateparser must be installed for today/yesterday.

approach_cards.name: Temporal IE strategy comparison (6 strategies, 5-axis judge)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Event SELECTION (which utterances are real temporally-grounded events) is harder than extraction quality; comparing modality-gating vs task-LLM vs multi-turn windows under an LLM judge reveals the best selection strategy.
approach_cards.method: 10h_ie_strategies.py + 10h_judge.py over 50 ctx0 turns. A=modality gate (spaCy), B=task-LLM (gpt-4o-mini), C=multi-turn 3-5 windows, D=linguistic pre-filter+selective (6 total). 5-axis: factuality, date provenance, entity density, noise ratio, coverage. OpenRouter gpt-4o-mini.
approach_cards.result: No final numeric winner recorded; key insight that event selection is harder than extraction quality.
approach_cards.notes: Motivated by MONTEE (modality tags), MAVEN-FACT (112,276 events, factuality tractable), EventWeave (core vs supporting), LED (conversational ≠ newswire), ConvLogMiner (3 detectors + voting).

approach_cards.name: Chronos reverse-engineering Phase A (Event Calendar + Dynamic prompting + Context expansion)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Replicating Chronos's dual-calendar design — separate FAISS Event Calendar (SVO state-transitions + ISO datetime ranges + aliases), per-question dynamic retrieval guidance, and ±1 turn context expansion — closes the gap to Chronos's 92.6%/95.6% LME SOTA (Event Calendar alone = 58.9% of Chronos's gain).
approach_cards.method: 3 modules: chronos_event_index.py (FAISS, search/grep/date_filter, query-conditioned selective SVO extraction by task LLM); chronos_dynamic_prompt.py (small LLM 1-5 guidance bullets/question); chronos_context_expansion.py (±k turn window, ±1 from same session on top-15 reranked).
approach_cards.result: All 3 BUILT, 49 Phase A tests passing (event 17 + dynamic-prompt 21 + context-expansion 11). Reference: Chronos Low (GPT-4o) 92.60%, High (Opus 4.6) 95.60%; our best then 31.33%.
key_numbers: ablations: no-init-retrieval -16.4, no-dyn-prompt -14.7, turns-only -12.9, no-rerank -12.1, no-date-filter -4.2
approach_cards.notes: Run Phase A tests separately — FAISS/spaCy segfault when mixed. Chronos uses TASK LLM (not specialized IE) for extraction, only temporally-grounded state transitions, query-conditioned. Modules built but not yet eval'd end-to-end at the 31.33% baseline.

approach_cards.name: Chronos reverse-engineering Phases B/C + dense-search correction (planned/architecture)
approach_cards.hypothesis: A 4-tool ReAct agent (search/grep × turns/events) over the dual calendars, plus 2-4 lexical aliases per event, completes the faithful Chronos reimplementation; correcting the early 'lexical-only' assumption to dense vector search (text-embedding-3-large on both calendars) was necessary.
approach_cards.method: Phase B planned chronos_agent.py (4 tools vs existing 7-tool structured_query.py, flag --chronos_agent). Phase C planned chronos_alias.py (2-4 variants/event). Architecture correction: Turn Calendar + Event Calendar both dense-embedded; pipeline = dynamic prompt → dense search top-100 → Cohere Rerank v3 top-15 → ±1 expand → ReAct.
approach_cards.result: Phases B/C TODO (not built). Dense-search understanding corrected — established the dual-calendar dense-retrieval design Phase A implements.
approach_cards.notes: Project MEMORY records ReAct agents ultimately HURT LME (-5 SubEM vs deterministic recall), so the agent direction was later superseded — here still planned. Early wrong lexical-only assumption would have produced a non-faithful reimplementation.

approach_cards.name: CL LoRA sweep — low-LR plateau (E01-E04, E10-E11, E14)
approach_cards.hypothesis: A small attention LoRA fine-tune injects conversation facts into a 1.5B model's weights; data format (raw/instruction/QA), more epochs, schedules, or moderate LR can match or improve injection.
approach_cards.method: Qwen2.5-1.5B on A40. E01 (lr=2e-4, r=16 attn, 3ep, raw) first working recipe; E02 SGD; E03 instruction fmt; E04 QA fmt; E10 lr=5e-4 8ep; E11 cosine schedule; E14 full-FT last-4-layers lr=5e-5.
approach_cards.result: All plateau ~4/60 (delta +3): E01 4/60, E03 4/60, E04 4/60, E10 4/60, E11 4/60, E14 4/60. E02 SGD 2/60 (worse). Baseline untrained = 1/60.
approach_cards.notes: Data format doesn't matter at low LR; epochs/cosine/moderate-LR can't substitute for the 1e-3 knife-edge; cosine 'kills high-LR zone too early.' SGD worse than AdamW here (opposite of TTT, where Adam destroys model). Full-FT first attempt LR too conservative.

approach_cards.name: E05 — LoRA r=16 attn, lr=1e-3, raw conv (BEST CL recipe, high variance)
approach_cards.hypothesis: A higher LR (1e-3) on attention LoRA pushes the model into the regime where it actually absorbs facts rather than just regularizing.
approach_cards.method: LoRA r=16 on attention, lr=1e-3, raw causal-LM on raw conversation. Qwen2.5-1.5B.
approach_cards.result: 10/60 SubEM (17%), delta +9. BEST of all 24 CL experiments. HIGH VARIANCE.
approach_cards.notes: lr=1e-3 is the 'knife-edge' — only value that injects; lower=stable ~4/60, higher/more-params=diverge. E22 rerun of SAME recipe got only 2/60 — stochastic, narrow, unreliable sweet spot.

approach_cards.name: CL LoRA destabilizers — QA/paraphrase/high-rank/MLP/clip/full-FT (E06-E09, E13, E15-E19)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Combining the winning lr=1e-3 with QA format, 10x paraphrase, rank-64, attn+MLP targeting, gradient clipping, full-FT, atomic-fact QA, or eval-time system prompts improves injection.
approach_cards.method: E06 QA+1e-3; E07 paraphrase+MLP LoRA; E08 paraphrase+attn; E09 rank-64; E13 grad-clip=1.0; E15 full-FT last-4 lr=1e-4; E16 attn+MLP lr=5e-4; E17 attn+MLP lr=1e-3; E18 atomic-fact QA (Knowledge-Instruct); E19 trained model + eval system prompt.
approach_cards.result: E06 5/60, E07 9/60 (degenerate output), E08 0/60 (diverged), E09 0/60 (diverged), E13 6/60 (too conservative), E15 7/60 (best full-FT), E16 6/60, E17 8/60 (diverged, false positives), E18 2/60 (diverged), E19 3/60 (hallucination not recall). None beat E05's 10/60.
approach_cards.notes: At 1e-3 raw>QA (QA destabilizes); paraphrase/rank-64/MLP at high LR diverge ('more capacity=instability', LoRA low-rank = implicit regularization); clip trades injection for stability; full-FT (~420M params) underperforms low-rank; E19 confirmed problem is ABSORPTION not generation. E18=Knowledge-Instruct (arXiv:2504.05571).

approach_cards.name: E20/E21 — MEGa gated per-event LoRA
approach_cards.hypothesis: One small LoRA adapter per event/session, gated at inference (MEGa), gives composable per-event memory that avoids interference.
approach_cards.method: E20: 43 per-session adapters, r=4, 3ep, top-1 gating. E21: 11 per-chunk adapters, r=16, 5ep, top-1 gating.
approach_cards.result: E20 3/60 (+2, adapters too small). E21 7/60 (+6, best MEGa). Still below monolithic E05 (10/60).
approach_cards.notes: MEGa = arXiv:2504.21239 (paper uses r=128). Architecture right, scale wrong — needs bigger model, higher rank, or external retrieval to gate.

approach_cards.name: E22 — refusal-direction ablation (RepE) on E05
approach_cards.hypothesis: Facts ARE stored but the model refuses to answer — ablating the refusal direction (Arditi et al.) would unlock recall.
approach_cards.method: E05 recipe + ablate refusal direction at inference (representation engineering).
approach_cards.result: 3/60 (+2); refusal ablation gave only +1 hit. Refusal is NOT the bottleneck.
approach_cards.notes: Refusal Direction = Arditi et al. NeurIPS 2024. Also a rerun of E05 that got only 2-3/60 vs 10/60 — proves E05 high variance. Problem is ABSORPTION not GENERATION.

approach_cards.name: E23 — Qwen2.5-7B, E05 recipe (scale-up)
approach_cards.hypothesis: A larger 7B model has more parametric capacity, so the E05 recipe should inject facts better.
approach_cards.method: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, same E05 recipe (lr=1e-3, LoRA r=16, 5 epochs).
approach_cards.result: 0/60, delta -3 (below baseline). Loss UP every epoch (6.15→7.22). Bigger = worse at lr=1e-3.
approach_cards.notes: 7B needs lower LR, but lower LR = no injection (per E10). LoRA fine-tuning for knowledge injection declared a DEAD END at current architecture.

approach_cards.name: Cumulative absorption + EWC (C-10a)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Cumulatively absorb all facts into a 0.5B model's weights, using Elastic Weight Consolidation to prevent catastrophic forgetting.
approach_cards.method: Sequential cumulative absorption into Qwen 0.5B + EWC penalty (Architecture J).
approach_cards.result: 9% probe accuracy. 33K facts overwhelm 0.5B.
approach_cards.notes: Weight-stuffing fails at scale — model can't hold 33K facts in 500M params. Motivated pivot to stateless-SLM + external-DB recursive oracle. (EWC+TTT and LoRA-per-conversation/progressive-capacity were listed as planned follow-ups but not executed.)

approach_cards.name: TTT-E2E h16 — v9 facts + absorb, SGD lr=1e-1, 50 steps, 50% dynamic (BEST CL result)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Per-query test-time weight adaptation on extracted v9 facts breaks the offline parametric ceiling — adapt weights at inference for each query.
approach_cards.method: TTT on Qwen anchor: pure absorption of top-k v9 facts, SGD lr=1e-1, 50 update steps, weight updates in 50% dynamic MLP layers (TTT-E2E style, final blocks), top_k=10.
approach_cards.result: 30% probe accuracy — 2.5x the offline ceiling (~12%). Best continuous-learning result.
approach_cards.notes: Pure absorption (30%) > QA-format (29%): model absorbs then answers from pretrained QA. v9 facts (30%) >> raw conversation (14%): extraction concentrates signal. Adam DESTROYS model at TTT LRs (0%) — SGD only.

approach_cards.name: Offline parametric architectures A-G
approach_cards.hypothesis: Various offline memory-augmentation architectures (hierarchical bank, ngram inject, MLA cross-attn memory, direct finetune) can store/recall facts without per-query adaptation.
approach_cards.method: 8 architectures registered in foundry/eval/parametric_research.py, evaluated offline (no test-time weight updates).
approach_cards.result: All offline architectures (A-G) cap at 12% probe accuracy. Only TTT breaks the ceiling.
approach_cards.notes: Mapped to MIRAS knobs: hierarchical_bank=neural/backprop; ngram_inject=hashtable/static-lookup; mla_memory=cross-attn/backprop; direct_finetune=weight-memorization. Missing knobs: attentional bias, retention gate, OGD.

approach_cards.name: JEPA-as-retrieval Phase 1 (injection variants: softprefix/textctx/FT/KV)
approach_cards.hypothesis: A JEPA world-model latent can serve fact recall — injected as a soft prefix, combined with text context, fine-tuned into the anchor, or pushed into the LLM's KV/self-attention cache.
approach_cards.method: jepa_v9_softprefix (001), jepa_v9_textctx (002), jepa_ft_cosine_lbd01 (003, λ=0.1 lr=5e-5 3ep), jepa_ft_realqa_lr1e5_ep1 (004), jepa_ft_lr1e5_ep2 (005), jepa_ft_lr1e5_ep3 (006), KV injection of JEPA state into self-attention (C-09).
approach_cards.result: 001 0.0% (prefix fails); 002 5.0% (encoder collapsed); 003 5.0% (overfit); 004 8.0% (qty 6/25); 005 13.0% (qty 10/25, best, beat 12% ceiling); 006 11.0% (3rd epoch regresses); C-09 4.0% (broke generation).
approach_cards.notes: Soft-prefix/KV inject of non-token-manifold vectors breaks generation (echoes Titans soft-prompt 0/60). JEPA encoder collapse: cosine 0.975, effective rank 30/256, self-retrieval 1/20; EMA target encoder does NOT prevent collapse. Best JEPA-FT (13%) barely beats ceiling, far below TTT 30% and sbert 65%.

approach_cards.name: C-JEPA / VICReg / contrastive on sbert (C-01 to C-07)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Adding VICReg variance+covariance and/or contrastive loss to JEPA — including on TOP of the strong sbert encoder, frozen, or dual-space — fixes collapse and beats sbert retrieval.
approach_cards.method: C-01 cjepa_vicreg05_individual; C-02 factlevel_vicreg05 (JEPA4Rec-style); C-03 sbert+JEPA+VICReg λ=0.5; C-04 sbert+C-JEPA+contrastive w=1.0; C-05 frozen-sbert + separate JEPA latent (dual, SCJEPA); C-06 sbert + JEPA re-ranker; C-07 frozen-sbert + pure contrastive head. ConversationJEPA _vicreg_loss() over sliding window of last 16 latents.
approach_cards.result: C-01 15.0%; C-02 12.0%; C-03 23.0% (best C-series, but DESTROYED sbert retrieval, loss 0.91→0.46 learned wrong thing); C-04 9.0%; C-05 18.0%; C-06 11.0%; C-07 14.0%. None recovered sbert's 65%.
approach_cards.notes: Post-mortem: JEPA optimizes PREDICTION (predict masked from context), retrieval needs DISCRIMINATION (find right fact for query). VICReg alone insufficient; contrastive+JEPA one swamps the other; any gradient update to sbert = catastrophic forgetting; MLP projection loses info (raw sbert > any projection). Closed Phase 1: 'JEPA for text is DEAD END.' VICReg=arXiv:2105.04906, C-JEPA=2410.19560, JEPA4Rec=2504.10512, SCJEPA=OpenReview KadCjvcLOz.

approach_cards.name: sbert retrieval baseline + k/encoder/anchor/prompt sweep (I-01 to I-08)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Embedding INDIVIDUAL facts (not grouped docs) with sbert and tuning top-k, encoder, anchor model, and grounding prompt maximizes fact-recall probe accuracy — the ceiling JEPA/TTT learning must beat.
approach_cards.method: Architecture I sbert over individual facts + text context, Qwen2.5-0.5B anchor. I-01 grouped 33-fact docs; I-01b individual k=10; I-02 k=5; I-03 k=20; I-04 mpnet k=10; I-05 k=8; I-06 k=15; I-07 Qwen3-0.6B anchor; I-08 'use ONLY facts' grounded prompt.
approach_cards.result: I-01b 65.0% (BEST of all 26 JEPA-phase exps); I-01 grouped 0.0%; I-02 56%; I-03 54%; I-04 mpnet 52%; I-05 58%; I-06 53%; I-07 Qwen3 52%; I-08 58%.
approach_cards.notes: Raw sbert retrieval >> any JEPA/MLP-projected latent. Data granularity: individual facts (65%) vs grouped docs (0%). k=10 sharp optimum (k=5 -9, k=20 -11). MiniLM>mpnet (-13). Qwen2.5-0.5B>Qwen3-0.6B anchor. 'answer concisely'>'use ONLY facts' (-7) — over-constraining 0.5B hurts. This is a RETRIEVAL result, the measured ceiling.

approach_cards.name: Titans / Neural Memory (Exp 1-6: ColBERT, surprise-weighting, soft-prompt, scratch MAC)
approach_cards.hypothesis: A Titans-style neural memory MLP (weights ARE memory) — using self-reconstruction or next-chunk-prediction surprise to weight ColBERT retrieval, or feeding MLP vectors as a soft prompt, or training a MAC transformer from scratch — beats the existing pipeline.
approach_cards.method: Exp1 ColBERT vs BM25 (no MLP); Exp2 sentence-level self-recon surprise + ColBERT; Exp3 token-level next-chunk surprise + ColBERT; Exp4 full MLP surprise-weighted ColBERT; Exp4b retrieve_memories() query expansion; Exp5 MLP→soft-prompt into Qwen2.5-1.5B; Exp6 45.7M-param MAC transformer from scratch on 380K tokens. LME ctx0.
approach_cards.result: Exp1 ColBERT 21/60 vs BM25 25/60 (-4); Exp2 21/60 (-4, surprise flat 0.3% range, 0 ranking changes); Exp3 20/60 (-5, 139x range, 55/60 changed but net negative); Exp4 23/60 (-1, best variant); Exp4b 21/60 (-3); Exp5 0/60 (-25, garbage); Exp6 4/60 (-21, PPL=40). Existing pipeline 48/60 best throughout.
approach_cards.notes: LME is keyword-heavy → exact-match BM25 beats fuzzy ColBERT. In 384-dim all chunks look similar (self-recon can't differentiate). Next-chunk surprise measures TOPIC TRANSITIONS not fact importance. MLP soft-prompt vectors off the token manifold → gibberish (same as JEPA softprefix/KV). 380K tokens can't learn English. Titans=arXiv:2501.00663.

approach_cards.name: NLCDM energy/Hopfield validation (N=1200 full scale + N=53 centroids)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Lean-proven NLCDM energy dynamics (transfer bound, energy descent, bridges, Hopfield retrieval) predict/improve real LME performance; coarse-graining to N=53 fact centroids (separated patterns) should satisfy proof assumptions and make it predictive.
approach_cards.method: 4 tests on all 300 LME Qs with real embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384d): transfer bound, energy-as-SubEM-predictor, bridges vs per-ctx SubEM, Hopfield vs cosine. Re-run on N=53 fact centroids. foundry/eval/test_nlcdm_energy.py.
approach_cards.result: N=1200: bound vacuously loose (1000x), δ NEGATIVE, ρ≈0.1; energy AUC 0.34-0.53, success/fail energy indistinguishable (-0.789 vs -0.790); bridges no correlation; Hopfield MRR -0.15 to -0.25 every ctx. N=53: δ POSITIVE +0.025, bound 54x, bridges meaningful — but AUC=0.40 non-discriminative, Hopfield MRR -0.19.
key_numbers: N=53 δ +0.025, bound 54x, AUC 0.40, Hopfield MRR -0.19
approach_cards.notes: Energy descent holds 100% (proofs correct) but vacuous at scale. Root cause: Hopfield energy = content-addressable retrieval (nearest stored pattern); LME requires REASONING over facts, not pattern completion. N=1200 dense turns violate small-N separated-pattern assumptions; even N=53 all queries converge to same basin. Valid math, wrong abstraction.

approach_cards.name: Recursive memory oracle — stateless SLM + external DB (double-loop)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Avoid catastrophic forgetting entirely: keep the SLM stateless, put memory in an external DB. Outer loop extracts/validates/links/stores; inner loop consolidates. The continuously-updated SLM becomes a queryable oracle for a bigger model.
approach_cards.method: Spec recursive-memory-oracle-spec.md; prototype foundry/eval/recursive_oracle.py. Outer: raw→extract→validate+link→store. Inner: consolidate (cross-ref, discover links, compress).
approach_cards.result: Proposed/prototyped as the answer to weight-stuffing failure (C-10a 9%, KV 4%). No SubEM in these files (oracle experiments tracked separately).
approach_cards.notes: Architecture validated by 'Sleeping LLM' (vbario, Feb 2026): SLM = stateless processor, DB = memory, no catastrophic forgetting. Per MEMORY, oracle enrichment later found NEUTRAL/dead-end for SubEM on ctx0.

approach_cards.name: Sleeping LLM (MEMIT wake + LoRA sleep) — referenced external architecture
approach_cards.hypothesis: Complementary Learning Systems for LLMs: MEMIT weight edits during 'wake' (short-term), LoRA consolidation during 'sleep' (long-term); sleep transfers MEMIT→LoRA then dissolves edits so capacity is unbounded — facts in weights, no retrieval/DB.
approach_cards.method: External work (vbario/sleeping-llm). Flagged MOST directly applicable (v9 facts → MEMIT triplets, same Llama-3.2-3B on RunPod). LoRA absorber + PEFT 0.19.1 patched on RunPod but NOT YET TESTED in our pipeline.
approach_cards.result: External results: Llama-3.1-8B → 100% recall @30 facts, PPL drift +3.2%. Wake capacity phase transition: 8B sustains 0.92 recall up to 13 edits, CRASHES at 14. Alignment tax (RLHF suppresses LoRA knowledge): 3B=47%, 8B=37%, 70B=0%.
approach_cards.notes: GitHub vbario/sleeping-llm (54 stars). Per-fact gating + cumulative fusing avoids alignment conflict. Not yet run in MIMIR's own pipeline (PEFT patched, untested).

approach_cards.name: Parametric-memory framework surveys (TTT-E2E landscape, MIRAS 4-knob, capacity theory)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Mapping test-time memory onto architecture surveys (dual-track static+dynamic TTT), the MIRAS 4-knob design space, and information-theoretic capacity limits identifies better designs and explains why weight-stuffing fails.
approach_cards.method: TTT-E2E survey (Stanford+NVIDIA Jan 2026: sliding-window attn + updates in final 25% MLP; In-Place TTT ICLR 2026 = final MLP as fast weights). MIRAS framework (Google Dec 2025, 4 knobs). Capacity numbers: 3.6 bits/param total (Meta May 2025), 2 bits/param factual (Allen-Zhu ICLR 2025), LoRA Capacity paper (arXiv:2502.14502).
approach_cards.result: TTT survey informed the in-house h16 30% experiment. MIRAS mapping: MIMIR covers only memory-arch + algorithm=backprop/static-lookup; MISSING attentional bias, retention gate, OGD. Capacity: 0.5B≈0.29GB facts, 3B≈6GB — explains 1.5B ceiling≈10/60 (17%) and 33K-facts-overwhelm-0.5B; ~500 facts/8B at lr=1e-3 rank=1.
approach_cards.notes: Theoretical backbone explaining empirical 1.5B≈10/60 ceiling and why E23 7B didn't trivially help. TTT-E2E open-source lib flagged highest-leverage open opportunity (4-8 wks); MIRAS knob explorer ranked #3 (3-6 wks). TTT-KV (arXiv:2602.21204): TTT = learned linear attention, NOT memorization.

approach_cards.name: Recursive Memory Oracle (enrichment, D-01..D-15)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Treat SLMs as stateless processors and the DB as memory (3 tiers: raw/structured/compressed); recursively enrich and re-retrieve evidence over recall() to lift hard (esp. preference) questions on ctx0.
approach_cards.method: OracleStore + oracle_enrich + oracle_retrieve (foundry/eval/recursive_oracle.py). 15 enrichment variants on ctx0 (60 Qs): graph retrieval (D-03 68.33%), RRF graph+BM25 (D-04 73.33%), structured fact prefix (D-06), graph traversal from 'user' (D-07b), stemming+block-only (D-08), full v9 cache no-gate (D-09), preference gate (D-10), embedding match type+items (D-11) vs items-only (D-12), top_k=40 (D-13), synthetic BM25 turns (D-14), always-on fact injection (D-15).
approach_cards.result: All ctx0 enrichment variants 80.00% (48/60) = recall() baseline D-06b 80.00%, OR regress: D-07b 75.00% (3 regressions, +10K garbage chars), D-09/D-15 75.00% (-3 factual), D-13/D-14 76.67% (-2). D-03 first real LME 68.33%, D-04 RRF 73.33% (still below 80%). Auto-probes pre-baseline (D-01) 86.0% was NOT real LME (rule violation); D-02 72.0% parser regression.
approach_cards.notes: Enrichment is a DEAD END on ctx0: SubEM is phrasing-hypersensitive, ANY text added to evidence drifts the answer. Adding ANY docs to BM25 (D-13/D-14) hurts precision. Only 6/60 preference Qs are enrichment targets; 4/6 already have correct evidence (generation problem). Spec: thoughts/shared/research/recursive-memory-oracle-spec.md.

approach_cards.name: Oracle NEI post-processing (D-16..D-18)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Post-processing (not evidence injection) — detect Not-Enough-Information cases via high-precision triggers and emit the exact gold refusal string — can produce a net SubEM gain on 5-ctx.
approach_cards.method: D-16 generic adjective+noun regex; D-16b high-precision triggers (quantity-unit-noun mismatch, named-entity comparison, sport/item type confusion); D-17 high-precision triggers + EXACT gold-format refusal ('The information provided is not enough. [reason]') + enhancement chain appending evidence suffixes to neutralize false positives; D-18 removes early-exit + adds Check 4 (entity mismatch).
approach_cards.result: D-16 65.67% (5-ctx, catastrophic false positives). D-16b 65.67% (correct triggers but SubEM format mismatch). D-17 66.00% (198/300) NEW 5-ctx BEST: 2 NEI rescues (30-gallon tank qty; autographed football vs baseball), 3 false positives neutralized. D-18 66.33% (199/300) NEW BEST but +1 is stochastic (9 gains/8 losses, Check 4 never fired). Per-ctx D-18: ctx0=48 ctx1=39 ctx2=38 ctx3=34 ctx4=40 (old cache).
approach_cards.notes: First oracle feature with a NET POSITIVE — and the ONLY thing that gained was POST-PROCESSING, not enrichment. Gold-format string matching was critical. D-18's +1 is LLM noise, not the new check. Ran on old cache (before ctx4 33%->98.8% v9 fix).

approach_cards.name: Oracle temporal computation (D-20)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Forward-propagate Chat Time markers to 100% chunk-timestamp coverage and compute date diffs (days/months ago) via the oracle as safe append-only post-processing.
approach_cards.method: Append computed temporal answers to enhanced_text (can't regress). Chunk-timestamp forward propagation + date diff.
approach_cards.result: Fired on 9/300, 0 rescues. NOT useful.
approach_cards.notes: DEAD END (DO NOT RETRY). Root cause: chunk timestamps = when an entity was DISCUSSED, not when the event HAPPENED ('bird watching 3 months ago' discussed in a May chunk -> infers 230 days; gold = 2 months). Recurring timestamp-vs-event-date confusion.

approach_cards.name: Oracle 5-ctx failure taxonomy
approach_cards.hypothesis: (Diagnostic) Characterize the ~101 remaining D-18 failures to locate the real bottleneck.
approach_cards.method: Manual failure analysis of 101/300 D-18 failures (and 102/300 post-D-17).
approach_cards.result: 59 long-gold preference (SubEM-bounded, need LLM-judge); 11 NEI (2 rescued by D-17); 31 short-gold retrieval misses = 100% of short-gold (21 temporal + 5 arithmetic); 1 format near-miss; 0 cases where gold IS in evidence but LLM fails.
approach_cards.notes: Decisive conclusion: ctx0 plateau is NOT generation (0 in-evidence failures) — it's RETRIEVAL coverage + a metric ceiling on preference Qs. Motivates LLM-as-judge + retrieval-coverage work, not more enrichment.

approach_cards.name: Code Oracle (Oracle-as-Code-Generator, bicameral)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Instead of LLM mental arithmetic, have an SLM generate Python from structured facts -> exec() -> deterministic answer; recover the 37 computational failures and replace ~500 lines of hardcoded English regex with a language-independent path.
approach_cards.method: research/REMem/test_oracle_bicameral.py over 5 question types (date diff, age diff, months, counting, sum); compared direct-answer vs code-gen for llama-3.2-3b and lfm2.5-1.2b. Wired as foundry/eval/code_oracle.py with _safe_exec() fix (pre-import datetime/math; previously silently returned []). Model qwen2.5-3b. Run on 5-ctx LME-S* and full LME-500.
approach_cards.result: Unit tests VALIDATED: code-gen 5/5 (llama-3.2-3b) / 4/5 (lfm2.5-1.2b) vs direct 2-3/5 (e.g. March15-March8=7, 75-32=43). 5-ctx +2 (181->183/300). LME-500 DEAD: 278/500 (55.6%) vs 280/500 baseline = net -2, 0 improvements, 2 regressions (Q101 overwrote '5 days' with refusal; Q459 added 'hiking' to 'GR-90 trail').
approach_cards.notes: Strictly dominates in unit tests; collapses on noisy large haystacks — SLM can't generate useful code from noisy evidence; appends corrupt already-correct answers. Rules out ALL code-generation answer post-processing. Decision: abandon, focus on retrieval.

approach_cards.name: Salience Engine (Fristonian/Kalman/particle math prototype)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Streaming per-token memory activation (memories fire BEFORE the query completes) gives zero retrieval latency at generation time via a pure-math active-set model.
approach_cards.method: v1 research/salience_prototype.py + v2 research/salience_engine_v2.py: Kalman filter (per-token surprise), particle filter (topic regime + resampling), Fristonian precision weighting (salience = precision x prediction_error x activation), exponential decay eviction, cascading Ashby/Beer variety attenuators (entity match -> temporal decay -> precision -> active set).
approach_cards.result: Math VALIDATED: recall@full = 20/20 (gold turn ALWAYS in active set 37-261, avg ~125), but RANKING broken — gold ranks 1-111 within the active set. Fristonian salience alone can't discriminate.
approach_cards.notes: Foundational diagnostic: recall PERFECT, ranking is the problem. Sets up the IDF-rerank fix. Math sound for candidate identification but blind to term rarity.

approach_cards.name: Salience raw ranking (Fristonian-only)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Rank the active set directly by Fristonian salience score (precision x prediction_error x activation), top-20.
approach_cards.method: Raw salience ranking, gpt-4o-mini generation via OpenRouter, 20-question LME set.
approach_cards.result: 4/20 (20%) SubEM. Q2 won by salience-only (broader candidate pool).
approach_cards.notes: Entity index is IDF-blind: common words ('work','daily') match as strongly as rare words ('coupon','IKEA'); Fristonian scoring can't discriminate. Recall perfect, ranking collapses.

approach_cards.name: Salience + IDF rerank (recall=salience, rank=IDF)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Split the two jobs: salience for RECALL (streaming candidate identification), BM25-style IDF for RANKING within the active set — fixes the IDF-blind ranking.
approach_cards.method: idf_rerank(): BM25-style IDF over only active-set candidates. Hybrid score = BM25 + 0.1 x salience (IDF dominates, salience tiebreaker); top-20. Optional SLM (lfm2.5-1.2b) cue expansion for vocabulary bridging.
approach_cards.result: 20q: 15/20 (75%) — +11 over raw salience (4/20), +1 over BM25 (14/20). 50q: 40/50 (80%) vs BM25 39/50 (78%). Salience-only wins 1 of each set; BM25-only wins 0. SLM bridging 11/12 adversarial tests pass (1.2B fails 'exercise'->'marathon'; 200-300ms/call, 2-15 calls/Q).
approach_cards.notes: Decisive fix: wider salience candidate pool gives IDF more correct options to surface. But batch gain over BM25 is marginal (+1/20). SLM cue expansion is a nice-to-have, NOT load-bearing. 50q run ~50min on MacBook (17K regex patterns x 500 turns, CPU bound). Real value claimed = streaming (per-token activation, decay) but UNMEASURED.

approach_cards.name: Semiotic memory — embedding-based (project 7-9 layers from vectors)
approach_cards.hypothesis: The 7 semiotic layers (Saussure/Peirce/Benveniste/Barthes/Derrida/Eco/Jakobson) can be recovered by partitioning/diffusing sentence embeddings (a 'denotative subspace').
approach_cards.method: v1 research/semiotic_diffusion_prototype.py: Gaussian noise (diffusion) on embeddings. v2: clean embeddings + Bayesian decay/update on random subslices. v3: BM25+cosine RRF + semiotic-layer reweighting.
approach_cards.notes: DEAD: embeddings have NO semiotic structure to project from. Gaussian noise destroys cosine (collapses to recency); Bayesian subslices pick wrong clusters; v3 classifies all queries 'referential' and semiotic weights kill the cosine signal. Baselines crushing every variant pivoted the line to LLM extraction.

approach_cards.name: Semiotic memory — extraction-based (LLM extracts 8-9 layers/turn)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Semiotic layers must be EXTRACTED via LLM analysis (LLMs have internalized semiotic theory from pretraining), enabling interpretive/non-retrieval queries impossible with flat retrieval.
approach_cards.method: research/semiotic_memory.py — gpt-4o-mini extracts 8 layers/turn (3-5s): Barthes denotation (=v9 facts + Peircean index/icon/symbol), Barthes myth, Saussure differential, Peirce sign+chain, Benveniste enunciation, Derrida absence, Eco encyclopedia, Jakobson function (+Husserl phenomenology 9th). Cross-session reconciliation detects contradictions/absences/myth evolution.
approach_cards.result: WORKS for INTERPRETATION (no SubEM): 'Am I lonely?' -> nuanced multi-layer synthesis (Derrida absence catches 'no loneliness mentioned despite living alone'); reconciliation detects contradictions/absences/evolution. This is interpretation, NOT retrieval — BM25 can never produce it.
