approach_cards.notes: Declared a DIFFERENT PROBLEM (interpretation, not retrieval); LME is the wrong benchmark. Claim: Semiotic SUBSUMES v9 (Barthes denotation = v9 facts; other layers add interpretive structure; one LLM call yields both). Latest research direction. semiotic-memory-research.md.

approach_cards.name: Semiotic query-time retrieval (entity-only + RRF)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Extracting semiotic entities at query time (entity-only match, or fused via RRF with BM25/cosine) would retrieve the right turns.
approach_cards.method: Entity-only retrieval and 8-layer-extraction+RRF, both at query time over the haystack. 10-question test, models lfm2.5-1.2b / qwen3.5-4b / gpt-4o-mini.
approach_cards.result: Entity-only: 1.2b 2/10, qwen3.5-4b 2/10, gpt-4o-mini 0/5. RRF: 1.2b 0/10, qwen3.5-4b 3/10, gpt-4o-mini 3/5 — ALL below each model's BM25 (1.2b 4/10, qwen3.5-4b 6/10, gpt-4o-mini 5/5).
approach_cards.notes: Root cause: extraction COVERAGE — only 5-15% of turns get extracted at query time. Conclusion: must PRE-EXTRACT at ingest (like v9 cache), not at query time.

approach_cards.name: Semiotic pre-extraction enrichment (BM25 top-20 then extract)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Retrieve BM25 top-20, then semiotically extract just those 20 turns to enrich without full-haystack cost; entity search also finds UPDATED (recency) values BM25 misses.
approach_cards.method: BM25 top-20 -> gpt-4o-mini semiotic-extracts those 20 turns; 15 hard Qs. Plus entity search on knowledge-update Qs.
approach_cards.result: BM25 raw 4/15 (26.7%) -> enriched 5/15 (33.3%), +1 Q (temporal 1/5->2/5; wins Q136 preference retrieval_tag, Q237 temporal when-fields). Entity-search knowledge-update wins: Q366 25:50 (correct updated PB) vs BM25 27:12 (old); Q367 4 restaurants (correct) vs BM25 3.
approach_cards.notes: Small but real lift, CAPPED by BM25 recall (can only enrich what top-20 retrieved). Entity indexing helps knowledge-update/recency Qs ONLY when extraction coverage is good — reinforces pre-extraction requirement. Next: entity index for recency-aware search.

approach_cards.name: hermes-memory Lean formalization (3 failure-mode fixes)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Three episodic-memory failure modes (lock-in, thrashing, cold-start starvation) each have a small dynamical-systems fix, and the three fixes COMPOSE at a unique globally stable equilibrium — provable in Lean 4.
approach_cards.method: Lean 4 (v4.29.0-rc2, Mathlib) across 6 files: MemoryDynamics, StrengthDecay (dS/dt=-betaS), SoftSelection (monotone sigmoid), NoveltyBonus (decaying exploration), ComposedSystem (Lipschitz), ContractionWiring (Banach capstone). Paired with hermes_memory/ Python Markov-chain Monte Carlo + spectral harness.
approach_cards.result: 75 theorems, 0 sorries. Capstone stableStationaryState_safe (unique stable equilibrium via Banach). Stability boundary derived: L*alpha*S_max < 1 - exp(-beta*Delta). 127 Python tests (22 files) confirm the deterministic fixed point holds stochastically and the contraction condition IS the real stability boundary.
approach_cards.notes: Fully sorry-free, self-validating (theorem + matching Monte Carlo). Validated as a CONTROL-THEORY result (memory-management dynamics), NOT shown to move SubEM. proofs/README.md, proofs/HermesMemory/.

approach_cards.name: hermes-NLCDM Lean formalization (15-phase coupled dynamics)
approach_cards.hypothesis: A Hopfield-inspired NonLinear Coupled Dynamical Memory (energy function + coupled updates) is a sound formal model of associative memory; Lyapunov stability, capacity, cross-domain transfer, bridge formation, and 4D authority composition can be proven AND should predict empirical retrieval.
approach_cards.method: Lean 4, 27 files across 15 phases (energy bounds, single-update Lyapunov, pairwise coupling, capacity, modular/block-diagonal, full-system stability, trace centroids/bridge formation, transfer/perturbation/emotional/hybrid/dream, authority monotonicity). Python: coupled_engine.py, dream_ops.py, nlcdm_core.py + MABench agent.
approach_cards.result: 260 theorems, 0 sorries, all 15 phases proven (energy descent holds 100% in proofs). BUT empirical validation NEGATIVE — see NLCDM energy validation record.
approach_cards.notes: Proofs complete and correct but empirically vacuous on the benchmark (separate record). proofs/HermesNLCDM/, coupled_engine.py.

approach_cards.name: NLCDM energy/Hopfield empirical validation on LME
approach_cards.hypothesis: The Lean-proved NLCDM theorems (Lyapunov energy descent, transfer bounds, bridge formation, Hopfield retrieval) should predict & improve LME — energy discriminates success/failure, Hopfield beats cosine.
approach_cards.method: Recovered 27-module proof library (0 sorry). 4 tests on all 300 LME Qs with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384d): transfer bound, energy-predicts-SubEM, bridges-vs-per-ctx-SubEM, Hopfield-vs-cosine. E24 retry on fact centroids (N=53). Scripts: foundry/eval/test_nlcdm_energy.py, test_nlcdm_energy_centroids.py.
approach_cards.result: PROOFS CORRECT, EMPIRICALLY VACUOUS. Transfer bound valid 100% but 1000x too loose (delta NEGATIVE at N>=1200, Spearman rho~0.1). Energy->SubEM AUC 0.34-0.53 (success vs fail energy indistinguishable: -0.789 vs -0.790). Bridges: no correlation at any tau. Hopfield strictly WORSE than cosine (MRR -0.15 to -0.25 every ctx). E24 centroids N=53: delta +0.025, bound 54x tighter, but AUC 0.40, Hopfield -0.19 MRR.
approach_cards.notes: DEAD END. N=1200 dense turns violate small-N/separated-pattern proof assumptions; even N=53 all queries converge to one energy basin. Hopfield = content-addressable retrieval; LME needs reasoning over facts — WRONG ABSTRACTION. Same failure mode as Triadic Memory.

approach_cards.name: MSL — Memory Specification Language (universal query DSL)
approach_cards.hypothesis: ALL retrieval (graph traversal, text search, temporal computation, aggregation) can be unified as first-class ops in one DSL; one LLM call extracts a structured DSLQuery, everything after is deterministic (no agentic loop, no fallback chains).
approach_cards.method: DSLQuery (op, entities, predicate, entity_type, temporal, params) + 15 ops across graph (lookup/multi_hop/count/sum/list/compare/yes_no/negation/preference/supersession), temporal (temporal/temporal_compute/temporal_filter), text (search_text/search_entity). 6-step deterministic ingestion (graph nodes/edges, co-occurrence, BM25, entity index, Allen intervals). Mapped to FacetEntity, multipass SVO, AllenORB (119 tests), EntityGraph.aggregate.
approach_cards.result: Synthetic: 86/86 tests pass, 0.16s, 0 API calls. Real LME 60 Qs: 17/60 (28.3%). Graph (19,549 entities, 66,389 facts, 6,311 types) answered 30/60 but ALL 30 WRONG (0/30) due to vocabulary mismatch (ingestion 'pet fish' vs query 'fish'); BM25 fallback rescued 17/30.
approach_cards.notes: CRITICAL lesson: vocabulary mismatch -> 100% graph failure; drove the 'unified pool / consistent extraction both sides' direction. Most formal/spec-like empirical artifact (analogue to the Lean arm). Predicate-dispatch + regex decomposition (no LLM) survived into foundry recall(). proofs/hermes-NLCDM/python/thoughts/.../plans/structured-retrieval/plan.md.

approach_cards.name: StructuredFactStore + QueryParser (3rd RRF channel) — spec
approach_cards.hypothesis: A dict-indexed (S,V,O) fact store (O(1) entity/predicate lookup) fused as a 3rd RRF channel beside BM25+entity_prefilter, driven by a regex-only (no-LLM) query parser, can close the gap toward Chronos-style structured retrieval (95.6%).
approach_cards.method: Planned mabench/structured_store.py (StructuredFact + 3 inverted indexes; position-aware scoring subj 5.0/obj 4.0/partial 2.0/pred 3.0, dedup-by-MAX) + query_parser.py (5 regex steps, <1ms target). Wired additively via RRF k=60, disabled by default. 5-phase plan, 22+ unit tests + discriminative integration on 1282-turn ctx0.
approach_cards.result: PLAN/SPEC ONLY. Targets: store alone >=50% hit@10 (vs BM25 58.3%, entity 60.0%); 3-channel >=65% hit@10; full LME SubEM >=25% (vs best 23.00%); no-regression-when-disabled; <1ms latency.
approach_cards.notes: Not realized as this exact module; the insight (predicate-dispatch, regex decomposition, index-at-ingestion) matured into foundry recall() and the turn-level BM25 fix. The 23%->90% framing was the gap; honest LME reached 60.33% (5-ctx) via the Engram path. plan.md under proofs/hermes-NLCDM/python/thoughts/.

approach_cards.name: Memory Router (regex + LLM-classifier versions) — spec
approach_cards.hypothesis: Replace a one-size-fits-all BM25 pipeline (31.33% SubEM) by routing questions to specialized strategies; biggest cheap win is indexing assistant turns (currently user-only). A regex router (0ms) or an 8B-classifier router (~116ms) dispatches; cascade fallback makes 76% raw accuracy ~98% effective.
approach_cards.method: Ground-truth audit of 300 LME Qs. Regex ROUTE_PATTERNS -> 6 strategies (fact retrieval, assistant recall, temporal engine, counting/aggregation, preference, refusal/confidence gate). LLM version: meta-llama-3.1-8b one-word classifier -> 5 categories + cascade. Ingestion: unified turn index (add assistant turns), Event Calendar, property-triple index.
approach_cards.result: PROJECTIONS, not realized eval. Regex signal accuracy: ASSISTANT_RECALL 100% (60), TEMPORAL_ORDER 100% (21), PREFERENCE 100% (22), COUNTING 94%, TEMPORAL_DURATION 62%. Projected 31.33% (94/300) -> ~52% (~155/300), +61 (assistant recall +23 easiest). LLM router 76% raw / 98% effective (confusion: fact 110, asst 28/30, temp 61/73, pref 29/30); projected staged 31.33% -> 53.00%, ceiling ~55-60%.
approach_cards.notes: Spec/projection only — early mabench-era pipeline pre-Engram. Preference (30 Qs) declared permanently SubEM=0 -> needs LLM-judge. Confidence gate worth ~13 free points on refusal Qs. Predicate-dispatch design survived into foundry recall().

approach_cards.name: Palantir-Foundry ontology research (entity-memory design influence)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Foundry's Ontology (object/property/link/action + structured ObjectSet queries) is a proven blueprint for structured entity memory; mapping it onto Hermes makes retrieval structured queries over typed entities, and its catalogued anti-patterns pre-empt KG-design mistakes.
approach_cards.method: Compiled a knowledge base from Palantir docs/Architecture Center/community + raw scrapes. Extracted 3 ontology layers, 6 core types, structured query model (ObjectSet filter chains, Search Around max-3-hops/10M-objects, aggregation), OAG vs RAG, HyDE patterns. Built explicit Foundry->Hermes mapping + 6-principle doctrine + 8 adopted anti-patterns.
approach_cards.result: Knowledge base + design tables. Mapping: Object Type=Entity type, Property=fact predicate+object, Link Type=typed edge, Action=supersession, Search Around=graph hop. 6 principles: index-at-ingestion/query-at-read; structured queries over text search; ENTITY is the query unit; typed directional relations; properties have history (supersession chain); universal schema. 8 anti-patterns adopted (God Object, Time Machine, Misnomer, etc.).
approach_cards.notes: Shaped the KG/faceted-ontology era (9 facets + 3-layer EntityGraph echo Object/Property/Link + stated/inferred/derived). 'index at ingestion, query at read' became core. Community caveat: Foundry Ontology != KG (no Cypher/variable-depth). KG/layered-graph later NET NEUTRAL for LME; only the structured-retrieval insight (predicate-dispatch, entity-as-unit) survived into recall(). proofs/.../palantir-foundry-knowledge-base.md.

approach_cards.name: Episodic-memory literature survey (EM-LLM / REMem / SEEM / Triadic)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Engram's weakness is not retrieval quality but BINDING — entities/relations/timestamps float free with no event frames, provenance pointers, or temporal contiguity. SOTA episodic systems reveal the missing index/binding layer.
approach_cards.method: Cloned & analyzed 4 systems: EM-LLM (ICLR 2025, surprise-based event segmentation + graph boundary refinement + temporal-contiguity buffer), REMem (ICLR 2026, 4-node/6-edge hybrid graph verbatim->gists->facts->entities + 5-tool agentic retriever), SEEM (arXiv:2601.06411, two-layer graph+frames + Reverse Provenance Expansion), Triadic Memory (3D binary SDR tensor). research/EM-LLM-model/, research/REMem/, research/TriadicMemory/.
approach_cards.result: EM-LLM LongBench avg 51.58 vs RAG 36.44 (pure KV-cache, no entity extraction). REMem LME overall EM 55.2% — but LLM-as-judge, NOT SubEM; our 66% SubEM already BEATS REMem. Triadic Memory = DEAD END (content-addressable like Hopfield, no temporal binding). Identified 3 missing pieces: event frames, provenance pointers, temporal contiguity (EM-LLM reserves 30% of context for block±1 neighbors).
approach_cards.notes: Core thesis: 'the fundamental problem is binding, not retrieval quality.' Directly motivated the EventFrame binding layer. Triadic Memory rejected as wrong abstraction (same failure later confirmed for NLCDM Hopfield).

approach_cards.name: Honcho architecture analysis (90%+ LME, deriver/dialectic/dreamer)
approach_cards.hypothesis: Understanding how Honcho reaches 90%+ on LME reveals whether NL-observation extraction can be ported to local SLMs.
approach_cards.method: Cloned plastic-labs/honcho. Analyzed deriver (NL observations), dialectic (agentic 5-tool answerer), dreamer (background deduction+induction consolidation), surprisal (geometric novelty on embedding trees).
approach_cards.result: Honcho 90.4% via: (1) NO schema extraction, NL observations only; (2) frontier LLMs everywhere (Gemini extraction, Claude reasoning); (3) 3-tier reasoning explicit->deductive->inductive; (4) agentic answering with 5 tools; (5) surprisal sampling. KEY: free-form NL works because frontier LLMs stay grounded; small models hallucinate with unconstrained output.
approach_cards.notes: Motivated the dual-extraction (schema->deriver) design: constrain the SLM's output space with schema so it can't hallucinate, recovering Honcho's NL benefits without frontier cost. Analysis, not an eval.

dead_ends.name: NLCDM Hopfield/energy formal-dynamics validation (full scale, N=1200)
dead_ends.why: Lean proofs correct (27 modules, 0 sorry, energy descent holds 100%) but empirically VACUOUS on 300 LME questions with real embeddings: transfer bound 1000x too loose, alignment gap delta NEGATIVE at N>=1200, Spearman rho~0.1; energy as SubEM predictor AUC 0.34-0.53 (success vs failure energy indistinguishable: -0.789 vs -0.790); bridges no correlation at any tau; Hopfield retrieval strictly WORSE than cosine (MRR -0.15 to -0.25 every context). Root cause: Hopfield energy is content-addressable pattern completion; LME needs reasoning over facts. Wrong abstraction. (cl-experiments.md, MEMORY.md)

dead_ends.name: NLCDM energy on fact centroids (N=53, E24)
dead_ends.why: Last attempt to rescue the energy theory at small N: delta finally POSITIVE (+0.025), transfer bound 54x loose (vs 1012x at N=1200), bridges semantically meaningful (american-airlines<->miami, delta<->jetblue). But AUC still 0.40 (<0.55, non-discriminative), Hopfield retrieval still MRR -0.19. All queries converge to one energy basin. Partial theory win, total practical failure. Confirmed dead end.

dead_ends.name: ReAct / agentic tool-calling retriever (AgenticRetriever, MABench FC port)
dead_ends.why: Agent HURTS for LME: -5 SubEM vs deterministic recall() and vs direct BM25. POC looked promising (38.3% BM25-only on 60q) but at scale the agent underperforms a single deterministic retrieval pass. Declared DEAD for LME.

dead_ends.name: Chronos-style pure tool-calling agent (h=3/h=5, +date-diff tool)
dead_ends.why: h=3 18.33% (-9.67% vs baseline), h=5 25.33% (-2.67%), hybrid+semantic_search 27.33% (ties), +compute_date_diff REGRESSED to 25.33% (-2.00%): temporal 19->18, multi-session 10->7. LLM uses 2-3 hops, rarely refines; event-selection (which dates to pass) is the bottleneck, not arithmetic. CLOSED.

dead_ends.name: Traces -> deterministic -> distilled SLM pipeline
dead_ends.why: Premise (distill the agent's traces into a small model) became moot the moment deterministic recall() beat the agent by 5 SubEM. Phases 2-4 never built.

dead_ends.name: LoRA continual-learning for knowledge injection (E01-E22, 1.5B)
dead_ends.why: 1.5B Qwen2.5 ceiling ~10/60 (17%, E05) and HIGH VARIANCE (rerun E22 got 2/60). LR=1e-3 is a knife-edge: lower = no injection (4/60), higher or more params = diverge (rank-64 E09 0/60, all-layer E17 false positives, atomic-QA E18 diverged). Data format irrelevant. Refusal is NOT the bottleneck (RepE ablation +1). The problem is ABSORPTION. At parametric capacity limit (~500 facts/8B; 1282 turns on 1.5B).

dead_ends.name: 7B continual-learning (E23, scale-up of E05 recipe)
dead_ends.why: Qwen2.5-7B at lr=1e-3: loss went UP every epoch (6.15->7.22), 0/60 after training (baseline 3/60) — WORSE than no training. Bigger model needs lower LR, but lower LR = no injection. LoRA knowledge-injection dead end at every scale.

dead_ends.name: Full fine-tune / high-rank / EWC weight-stuffing
dead_ends.why: Full FT last-4-layers best only 7/60 (E15). Cumulative absorption + EWC = 9% probe (C-10a): 33K facts overwhelm the 0.5B model. Capacity analysis: 0.5B ~ 0.29GB fact capacity. More capacity = instability, not better recall.

dead_ends.name: MEGa gated per-event LoRA adapters (E20/E21)
dead_ends.why: Architecture right, scale wrong: 43 tiny r=4 adapters 3/60 (each sees too little data); 11 bigger r=16 adapters 7/60 — still below monolithic E05's 10/60. Needs a bigger model or retrieval-guided gating to pay off.

dead_ends.name: Offline parametric architectures A-G
dead_ends.why: All 8 offline (non-test-time) parametric memory architectures cap at 12% probe accuracy. Only per-query weight adaptation (TTT) breaks the ceiling. Static parametric memory insufficient.

dead_ends.name: JEPA world-model into LLM (KV-injection C-09, soft-prefix jepa_v9_softprefix 001)
dead_ends.why: KV-injection 4% probe accuracy, broke generation. Soft-prefix 0.0%. JEPA latent as a prefix/KV is not a valid token representation; the LLM cannot consume it.

dead_ends.name: C-JEPA / VICReg encoder training for retrieval (C-01..C-07)
dead_ends.why: JEPA's prediction objective != retrieval metric. Best C-series 23% (C-03) but JEPA training DESTROYED sbert's retrieval (loss converged 0.91->0.46 so it LEARNED, but learned the wrong thing). Contrastive+JEPA (C-04) 9% (one objective swamps the other). All variants 9-23% vs sbert baseline 65%. JEPA encoder collapses on short facts.

dead_ends.name: Titans / Neural Memory (ColBERT + surprise-weighted MLP)
dead_ends.why: ColBERT worse than BM25 for keyword-heavy LME (21 vs 25/60, -4). MLP surprise weighting: best variant 23/60 (still -1 vs BM25, far below 48/60 pipeline). Soft-prompt MLP->LLM 0/60 (garbage, vectors aren't token embeddings). MAC-from-scratch 4/60 (can't learn English, PPL=40). Whole family below plain BM25.

dead_ends.name: Recursive memory oracle enrichment (D-05..D-15)
dead_ends.why: NEUTRAL on ctx0: D-05 through D-12 ALL 80.00% = identical to recall() baseline (D-06b). Graph traversal from 'user' (D-07b) HURTS: prepends ~10K garbage chars, 3 regressions. Full v9-cache injection (D-09/D-15) HURTS factual Qs (-3). Embedding match (D-11/D-12): right blocks found but model ignores them. Only 6/60 preference Qs are enrichment targets and 4/6 are generation-quality, not retrieval, problems.

dead_ends.name: Oracle temporal computation (D-20)
dead_ends.why: Fired on 9/300, 0 rescues. Chunk timestamps = when an entity was DISCUSSED, not when the event HAPPENED. 'bird watching 3 months ago' discussed in a May chunk -> oracle infers May start -> '230 days' when gold is '2 months'. Discussed-date != event-date kills it. NOT RUN beyond diagnosis.

dead_ends.name: Code oracle (oracle-as-code-generator) on LME-500 / 5-ctx
dead_ends.why: Validated in isolation (llama-3.2-3b code-gen 5/5 vs 2-3/5 in-head) but DEAD at benchmark scale. LME-500: 278/500 vs 280/500 baseline = net -2, ZERO improvements, 2 regressions (Q101 overwrote correct '5 days' with a refusal; Q459 appended 'hiking' to 'GR-90 trail' breaking SubEM). On 5-ctx only +2. SLM can't generate useful code from noisy haystack evidence; oracle text corrupts already-correct answers.

dead_ends.name: Hard-coded regex computation (temporal-diff / arithmetic / quantity-sum)
dead_ends.why: Inflated 5-ctx from 181 to 196/300 — 15 of those correct answers came directly from regex computing the answer, not from memory. Removed for honest eval (_infer_temporal_diff, _infer_arithmetic, _infer_quantity_sum deleted). Benchmark-gaming, not a memory capability.

dead_ends.name: Dual extraction observations as BM25/vector evidence at ctx0
dead_ends.why: ALL 4 variants HURT vs 48/60 baseline (45-46/60). 5913 observations vs 1282 turns = 82% of the vector index becomes observations, displacing the real evidence the LLM needs. Counting regressed (qi=39 'how many days' 17->8). SLM deriver 1078s and WORSE than template. (The pivot 'search observations, serve turns' is a different, pointer-based architecture.)

dead_ends.name: Free-form / unbounded-ontology triple extraction
dead_ends.why: 190 ad-hoc entity types, predicate fragmentation, 1.7% SubEM on 54K triples. Unbounded vocabulary makes facts unretrievable: the query predicate never matches the extraction predicate. Motivated the bounded faceted schema.

dead_ends.name: Typed-graph / MSL structured query as primary retrieval
dead_ends.why: MSL graph (19,549 entities, 66,389 facts) answered 30/60 LME Qs but ALL 30 WRONG (0/30 correct) due to ingestion-vs-query vocabulary mismatch ('pet fish' vs 'fish'). Pure structured_query 21.00% (-7% vs BM25). Structured store as 3rd RRF channel NEUTRAL (22-23%, within noise). Can't replace BM25; only additive as a refusal-only fallback.

dead_ends.name: REBEL knowledge-graph extraction / supersession
dead_ends.why: Costs 10 SubEM points (29 with REBEL vs 39 without). seq2seq GENERATES property labels -> hallucinates; parser bug swaps relation/object. F1=93 on NYT but disabled for honest eval. Benchmark-advantaged. Do not retry with other RE models.

dead_ends.name: spaCy / OpenIE dependency-parse triple extraction
dead_ends.why: ~45 unique (S,P) keys from 18K facts = essentially empty graph, orders of magnitude too sparse. English-only SVO, not cross-lingual. OpenIE alternative gave 13K edges but too noisy. Insufficient graph density.

dead_ends.name: Cross-encoder reranker (with or without entity_prefilter)
dead_ends.why: xenc alone adds nothing on LME (17.33% = BM25+xenc). WITH entity_prefilter CATASTROPHIC: 17.00% vs 22.67% = -5.67% (-17 questions) — entity RRF already found the right docs, xenc reshuffles correct results OUT of top-k. Qwen3-Reranker-4B Hit@5 19% (dead). Never combine xenc with entity_prefilter. (mxbai-rerank over RRF top-30 was the only reranker that helped.)

dead_ends.name: Hard entity-first / entity-primary retrieval
dead_ends.why: Hard entity filtering = SubEM 9 catastrophe. --entity_primary 15.00% vs BM25 16.67%; 72.2% hit@10 was MISLEADING (finds topically-relevant not exact matches: F1 up, SubEM down). The bottleneck is LLM selection, not retrieval. Only usable as a soft (0.1x) RRF supplement.

dead_ends.name: Retrieval over-fetch / wider top_k / smaller top_k
dead_ends.why: Over-fetch 30-50 facts: SubEM 24-26 (noise dilution). top_k=40 (D-13) -2. retrieve_num=3: 24.67% vs 31.33% (-6.66%, recall loss). Reversed evidence (exp125/154) -3/-4. Truncated evidence (exp155) -3. char_budget=20000 (exp105) -2. top_k=20 / top10 / full best-first evidence is the sweet spot; LLM needs full context, best-first.

dead_ends.name: Cosine dedup / recency-first sort / batch dream consolidation
dead_ends.why: Cosine dedup (any threshold) SubEM 19-23: geometry can't tell conflicts from template similarity. Recency-first sort SubEM 5 (catastrophic): recency only works WITHIN conflict groups. Batch 'dream' consolidation SubEM 5-15: only longitudinal/online consolidation works.

dead_ends.name: Larger chunk sizes (cs1024 / cs2048)
dead_ends.why: Monotonic regression: cs512 28.00% -> cs1024 26.67% -> cs2048 25.33%. Bigger chunks = more noise per retrieved doc, retrieval_ok_answer_wrong grows monotonically. cs512 optimal.

dead_ends.name: Temporal pre-filter / event-calendar RRF channel / date-arithmetic short-circuit
dead_ends.why: Date-window BM25 (all sizes) ties plain BM25 (58.3% hit@10, zero added value); entity+temporal intersection WORSE (46.7%, narrows too much). Event-calendar as 3rd RRF channel 27.00% vs 28.00% (redundant with BM25). date_arithmetic fires 26/26 temporal Qs but ALL wrong (extract_event_date picks conversation date not event date). Temporal short-circuit 40% (10/25). 3-feature temporal stack regressed targets. Should filter retrieval, not the answer; date extraction confuses discussed-date with event-date.

dead_ends.name: Omni-SimpleMem techniques (exact_words_prompt, set_union_merge)
dead_ends.why: exact_words_prompt -1.33% (LLM over-quotes irrelevant fragments). set_union_merge -1.00% (BM25+entity RRF beats set-union; entity channel deserves fair RRF ranking, not relegation). Both stacked -3.00%. Paper's findings (OpenAI embeddings, shorter contexts) don't transfer to LME.

dead_ends.name: Prompt-framing / role-weighting / temperature tweaks
dead_ends.why: Conversation-framing fix ('history chats'->'conversation history') net -4 (LLM refuses more). Role weighting (assistant 0.7) = baseline, no help. Temperature 0.7 hurts SubEM (randomness). Dynamic prompting alone +0.33% (1 question = LLM nondeterminism). Combo of negatives stacks. raw_chunks deterministic best-first is the ceiling.

dead_ends.name: Semiotic memory — embedding-based (project 7 layers from vectors)
dead_ends.why: Improved only 1/15 -> 3/15 -> 5/15; both cosine and BM25 baselines hit 9/15. Embeddings have NO semiotic structure to project layers from. v1 noised-embeddings (diffusion) 1/15 (Gaussian noise destroys cosine -> pure recency). v2 clean+decay 3/15. v3 RRF+semiotic weighting 5/15 (weights kill the cosine signal). Query-time entity/8-layer extraction also catastrophic (gpt-4o-mini 0/5) due to 5-15% turn coverage. NOTE: extraction-based semiotic WORKS for interpretation ('Am I lonely?'), just not for SubEM retrieval.

dead_ends.name: Salience engine — Fristonian salience as ranker
dead_ends.why: Raw Fristonian salience (precision x prediction_error x activation) 4/20 (20%) — recall is perfect (gold always in active set) but ranking is broken (gold ranks 1-111). Salience+IDF rerank reaches 15/20 (75%) but that's only +1-2 over standalone BM25 (14/20, 39/50). The batch case for salience over BM25 is a single question; rests entirely on unmeasured streaming benefits. SLM cue expansion (1.2B) can't bridge 'exercise'->'marathon'.

dead_ends.name: Triadic Memory (3D SDR tensor) — external prior art
dead_ends.why: Operates on SDRs not embeddings, still content-addressable, no temporal binding. Same wrong-abstraction failure as Hopfield: LME needs reasoning over facts, not closest-match recall. Not adopted.

dead_ends.name: Residual-stream entity-position retrieval (KV-Direct)
dead_ends.why: v1 a strawman; v2 AUC=1.000 but only fact-to-fact (identical text), misleading. v3 definitive: in-context layer-14 cos useless (template context bleeds, all countries 0.987-0.994, gap 0.006); isolated-entity layer-14 best but gap only 0.134 and effective rank 56/1024 (5.5%). Query-to-fact retrieval from residual stream doesn't carry usable semantics; KV-compression claim doesn't translate to a working retriever.

dead_ends.name: ADELIE-SFT-1.5B event extraction
dead_ends.why: DEAD, do not use: best prompt only 37.5% (3/8); v3_simple 0/8. The 3B variant got 100% (8/8) on the same prompt, so 1.5B is below the usable extraction floor for this task.

dead_ends.name: Llama 3.1 8B as faceted extractor
dead_ends.why: 80% hallucination rate — DO NOT USE. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is the chosen extractor (3% hallucination). Raw-text deriver on 3B/7B also hallucinates (injects parametric knowledge in free-form output); only schema-constrained (schema->deriver) extraction is grounded.

dead_ends.name: v9 prompt extraction at production speed
dead_ends.why: 8065-char 6-step prompt: 40s/chunk on A40, 27% timeouts — UNUSABLE (LME-500 estimate 145h). Output overflows. Replaced by 299-char lightweight prompt: 1.7s/chunk, clean JSON. (H200 with 32 workers + prefix caching later hit 1.2 chunks/s.)

dead_ends.name: Intent routing / keyword-based query routing
dead_ends.why: Project directive: everything always-on, no keyword-based routing. Gating post-processing on question keywords fails multilingual (English triggers break on other languages). Gate on prediction/evidence patterns (regex on OUTPUT), never on question keywords.

formal_proofs.result: VERIFIED-COMPILED, empirically validated for its scope. 6 Lean proof files (HermesMemory.lean + ComposedSystem, ContractionWiring, MemoryDynamics, NoveltyBonus, SoftSelection, StrengthDecay), git-tracked and present as 7 compiled .olean artifacts in .lake/build/lib/lean/HermesMemory/ (compilation evidence). 75 theorems, 0 sorries (per project memory; working-tree .lean source is committed as empty stubs, content survives only as oleans). Capstone is a Banach fixed-point argument: the three failure-mode fixes (strength decay anti-lock-in, soft selection, cold-start survival) compose at a UNIQUE STABLE equilibrium. Derived stability boundary L*alpha*S_max < 1 - exp(-beta*Delta) (decay gap must dominate selection-feedback amplification). EMPIRICALLY VALIDATED: 127 Python tests across 22 test files confirm the deterministic fixed point holds stochastically and that the contraction condition is the REAL stability boundary — violating it causes convergence failure.
formal_proofs.theorems: stableStationaryState_safe (capstone, Banach fixed-point composing the 3 fixes at the unique stable equilibrium); steadyState_lt_Smax (strength plateaus below max, anti-lock-in); softSelect_monotone_score (higher score => higher selection probability); coldStart_survival (new memories survive the exploration window); composedSystem_safe (all three guarantees hold simultaneously)

formal_proofs.result: VERIFIED-COMPILED but empirically VACUOUS at LME scale. 27 Lean proof modules (HermesNLCDM/*), git-tracked and present as 28 compiled .olean artifacts in .lake/build/lib/lean/HermesNLCDM/ (compilation evidence; theorem names like lyapunov_strict_descent, energy_descent_strict, coupled_descent_pairwise extracted directly from the oleans). 260 theorems, 0 sorries across 15 proof phases (per project memory; working-tree .lean is empty stubs). All 15 phases proven sorry-free: Lyapunov full-system stability (phase 6), bridge formation (7-9), cross-domain transfer (10-14), 4D authority/importance-monotonicity capstone (phase 15). PROOFS ARE CORRECT — energy descent / Lyapunov convergence holds 100% in-proof. EMPIRICAL VALIDATION FAILED on 300 LME questions with real embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384d): (1) transfer bound valid 100% but 1000x too loose, alignment gap delta NEGATIVE at N>=1200, Spearman rho~0.1; (2) energy as SubEM predictor AUC 0.34-0.53, success vs failure energy indistinguishable (-0.789 vs -0.790); (3) bridges no SubEM correlation at any tau; (4) Hopfield retrieval strictly WORSE than cosine, MRR -0.15 to -0.25 every context. Fact-centroids retry (N=53): delta +0.025, bound 54x tighter, bridges semantically meaningful — but AUC still 0.40, Hopfield still -0.19 MRR. CONCLUSION: valid math, wrong abstraction — Hopfield energy is content-addressable pattern completion; LME requires reasoning over facts. Dead end.
formal_proofs.theorems: lyapunov_nonincreasing / lyapunov_strict_descent / energy_descent_strict / not_equilibrium_energy_decreases / coupled_descent_pairwise (phase 6, verified present in Lyapunov.olean); BridgeFormation, TransferDynamics, TraceCentroid (phases 7-14); AuthorityMonotonicity 4D capstone (phase 15)

families.name: Agentic / ReAct Retrieval
families.description: Tool-calling agents that iteratively retrieve evidence via multi-step reasoning loops — the MABench/FC monolithic winner (cooc+triadic+decompose+CR+bm25_hops, SubEM 39), the composed-agent refactor, the 7-tool AgenticRetriever, the Chronos tool-calling agents (h=3/h=5), and the planned Traces→Deterministic→Distilled-SLM pipeline.
families.arc: Started as the project's first serious system in the MABench era (March, SubEM 39 best on FactConsolidation). A POC on LME looked promising (38.3% BM25-only). But once a single deterministic recall() function was built, the agent measured -5 SubEM against it (and vs direct BM25); every Chronos agent variant tied or regressed against plain chunks. ABANDONED for LME — 'agent HURTS', declared dead. The trace-distillation follow-on was rendered moot before phases 2-4 were built.

families.name: Engram / Foundry Retrieval (recall() core)
families.description: The hybrid-retrieval workhorse: a single recall() function doing BM25 + cosine RRF + cross-encoder rerank, with turn-level (not chunk-level) BM25 indexing, predicate dispatch, reranker ablation (mxbai winner, Qwen3-Reranker dead), chunk-size and aggregation-overflow sweeps, and the long exp1xx micro-experiment series.
families.arc: Emerged as the foundation around 2026-04-20 after the structured-store era stalled, immediately delivering 43.33% ctx0. Turn-level BM25 closed a 35-point gap with MABench and became standard. Component ablation proved ranking was SOLVED (mxbai puts 97.2% reachable in top-10) and recall was the bottleneck (53% unreachable). Micro-experiments (exp147-155, evidence-order/truncation/top_k) all plateaued or regressed — the configuration space was exhausted. WON: this is the canonical system that hit 60.33% honest 5-ctx (#1 on LME(S*) leaderboard) and 56% on LME-500. Folded every other family's gains in or out around it.

families.name: Structured / Knowledge-Graph Retrieval
families.description: Entity- and triple-based retrieval as an alternative or supplement to text search: StructuredFactStore as a 3rd RRF channel, entity-prefilter, KnowledgeGraph (rustworkx PPR), HyperedgeIntersection, hard entity-first filtering, the bottom-up 14-op KG Query Engine, MSL query DSL, and the Palantir-Foundry ontology influence.
families.arc: A dominant March-April thrust. Entity-prefilter was a genuine win (+6%, the 22.67% jump). But pure structured query replaced BM25 badly (-7%), the structured store was net-neutral across Exp A/B/C (~22%), hard entity-first filtering caused the SubEM=9 catastrophe, and the MSL graph answered 30/60 questions ALL WRONG due to ingestion-vs-query vocabulary mismatch. FOLDED-IN as a supplement only (hybrid BM25 + structured fallback reached 31.33%); the standalone-graph dream was ABANDONED — the entity is sound as a unit but extraction-vocabulary consistency was the unbreakable blocker.

families.name: Information Extraction & Ontology Design
families.description: Turning conversation into structured facts: spaCy/REBEL/GLiNER2/textacy extractors, QA-driven 5W1H extraction, the 28-relation-type schema, the 9-facet shape-based ontology, layered EntityGraph (STATED/INFERRED/DERIVED), the v9 Qwen2.5-7B pipeline, and the dual-extraction (schema→deriver) architecture.
families.arc: A relentless reduce-hallucination, increase-density campaign. Early IE failed hard: REBEL cost -10 points and swapped relation/object; spaCy gave only 45 unique (S,P) keys; free-form extraction got 1.7% SubEM. The 9-facet ontology + grounding substring check fixed the design (graph = user's words). v9 reached 97.2% entity grounding after the source_text fix (16%→92%). The breakthrough was dual-extraction: schema constrains the deriver so even a 3B model hallucinates zero. WON as architecture (production path: lightweight prompt, 1.7s/chunk), though the layered/typed graph stayed net-neutral on SubEM because of vocabulary mismatch.

families.name: Temporal Information Extraction & Reasoning
families.description: Date and event handling: Allen interval algebra engine, stateful MSL schema with sub_role, the always-on temporal pipeline (Chat-Time ingestion, proximity re-ranking, code-computed deltas), ADELIE event-extraction prompts, regex date ceilings, _infer_temporal_diff, and the Chronos dual-calendar Event Calendar.
families.arc: Recognized early as the hardest LME category (35% on LME-500). Many naive attempts failed: temporal pre-filter added zero value, the 3-feature stack regressed, temporal short-circuit hit only 40%, and date-arithmetic modules 'fired on 26/26, all wrong' because chunk timestamps mark when an event was DISCUSSED not when it HAPPENED — the central, recurring failure mode. WON in narrow form: stateful MSL hit 100% multilingual, and code-computed _infer_temporal_diff drove ctx0 to 80%. PARTIALLY FOLDED-IN; the deeper temporal-reasoning gap remains the #1 open bottleneck (79% of temporal failures are retrieval misses).

families.name: Episodic Memory & Event Binding
families.description: Adding an event/episode index layer over content-addressable retrieval: EventFrames (topic-shift segmentation + temporal contiguity), and the prior-art survey of EM-LLM, REMem, SEEM, and Triadic Memory framed around content-addressable-vs-index-based memory.
families.arc: A late-April direction sparked by literature survey. The survey crystallized 4 ranked missing capabilities (temporal contiguity, event gists, provenance pointers, surprise segmentation) and the framing that 'our system is 100% content-addressable, needs an index layer'. EventFrames were fully built (47 tests, 5 contract assertions pass) but eval was exactly NEUTRAL — 196/300, matching baseline to the question. FOLDED-IN as correct infrastructure that didn't move SubEM; episodic binding is in place but score-neutral, awaiting the provenance/gist modalities to pay off.

families.name: Dual Extraction & Observations
families.description: Generating natural-language observations from verified schema and using them as a semantic-search modality, culminating in the 'Search Observations, Serve Turns' pointer architecture where observations bridge retrieval gaps but raw turns are served as evidence.

First direct use FAILED at ctx0: observations in the index displaced real turns (82% of vector index became observations) and regressed counting. The insight was to decouple — search observations, resolve to source turn IDs, serve turns. IN-PROGRESS at project end (LME-500 eval running against 280/500), motivated by the finding that 79% of LME-500 failures are retrieval misses that denser observations might bridge. The most-alive non-retrieval research thread at close.

families.description: Writing memory into model weights rather than an index: 24 LoRA/full-FT experiments (E01-E24), MEGa gated per-event adapters, Test-Time Training, Titans/neural-memory, the Hebbian bridge, MIRAS/MIRROR design frameworks, parametric-capacity theory, and the Sleeping-LLM (MEMIT wake + LoRA sleep) reference.
families.arc: The core JEPA/engram research mandate (learning, not retrieval). Brutal across the board: best LoRA was E05 at 10/60 (17%, high variance), bigger models DIVERGED (E23 7B: loss up every epoch, 0/60), Adam destroyed the model, EWC-at-scale hit 9%, all Titans variants regressed. Capacity theory explained why (0.5B ≈ 0.29GB, 33K facts overwhelm it). The one bright spot: TTT broke the 12% offline ceiling at 30% via per-query weight adaptation. Largely ABANDONED for LME (parametric learning a dead end at this scale), but TTT-E2E flagged as the highest-leverage open opportunity.

families.description: JEPA/C-JEPA/VICReg latent-prediction approaches to memory: ConversationJEPA sliding-window latents, JEPA soft-prefix and KV injection, JEPA fine-tune variants, contrastive/dual-space heads, and sbert retrieval baselines (Architecture I) used as the control.
families.arc: Pursued under the continuous-learning mandate as world-models for multi-hop structure. Consistently FAILED: soft-prefix 0%, KV injection 4% (broke generation), every C-JEPA/VICReg variant 9-23%, and crucially JEPA training DESTROYED sbert's retrieval (loss converged but learned the wrong thing — prediction objective ≠ retrieval metric). The control quietly won: plain sbert over individual facts hit 65%, the best of all 26 JEPA-phase experiments. ABANDONED — JEPA's predictive objective is the wrong abstraction for fact retrieval.

families.name: Formal Verification (Lean) & Energy Dynamics
families.description: The formal half of MIMIR: Lean 4 proofs of memory dynamics — hermes-memory (75 theorems, Banach fixed-point stability), hermes-NLCDM (27 modules, 260 theorems, 15-phase coupled dynamics, all sorry-free), and the empirical NLCDM/Hopfield energy validation on real LME embeddings.
families.arc: Built first (Feb-March) as the project's formal foundation and remained mathematically pristine: 0 sorries throughout, energy descent / Lyapunov stability holds 100% in proofs, with a derived stability boundary. But empirical validation (April) was a DEAD END: at LME scale (N=1200) the transfer bound was 1000x too loose, energy couldn't distinguish success from failure (AUC 0.34-0.53; -0.789 vs -0.790), and Hopfield retrieval was strictly worse than cosine everywhere. Even fact-centroids (N=53) didn't rescue it. PROOFS CORRECT BUT VACUOUS — Hopfield energy is content-addressable recall; LME needs reasoning over facts.

families.name: Post-Processing, Routing & Evaluation Methodology
families.description: Everything between retrieval and score: the recursive memory oracle (D-01 to D-20, SLMs as stateless processors), the code-generator oracle, NEI detection, evidence-gate widening, the memory router (regex and LLM-classifier), dual-tier LLM-as-judge scoring, and eval-integrity work (hard-coding removal, ground-truth bug discovery).
families.arc: A pragmatic late thread once retrieval plateaued. The recursive oracle was NEUTRAL on ctx0 (D-05 to D-12 all exactly 80%, matching baseline) — enrichment a dead end — but post-processing NEI detection (D-17/D-18) did become 5-ctx best (66.33%). The code oracle worked in isolation (5/5) but was KILLED on LME-500 (0 improved, 2 regressed). The router was validated (98% effective accuracy) projecting 31%→53%. Critically, this family enforced honesty: hard-coded regex computation was REMOVED (196→181/300), and the resulting 60.33% honest baseline still topped the LME(S*) leaderboard. WON as the discipline that kept results trustworthy; the oracle/router pieces mostly folded-in selectively or stayed projected.

eras.label: Era 1 of 5
eras.title: The Energy Well: Building a Memory from First Principles
eras.narrative_md:
The first week of MIMIR was an act of faith in mathematics. The question I set out to chase was almost arrogant in its ambition: could a long-term memory for an AI be *derived* — proven correct from physical first principles — rather than merely engineered and tuned until the benchmark numbers looked good? Most memory systems are scaffolding held up by hyperparameters. I wanted bedrock.

So I began with the scaffolding anyway. The first three days (Feb 27–28) were a TDD sprint to build hermes-memory v1: five modules — encoding, recall, contradiction, consolidation, optimizer — each one hardened by adversarial pre-passes before a line of implementation was written. Recall got score-gap adaptive-k depth selection instead of a lazy fixed top-k. Contradiction came out at 1,457 lines after three adversarial passes surfaced 39 findings. Consolidation's build was where the discipline paid for itself: a cascade analysis traced a 24x over-retention bug back to a single hours-vs-days unit confusion (C2). The system had been *functionally broken at the dynamics level* and the tests caught it. By the time the orchestrator (770 lines) wired all five modules together, the suite stood at **1,455 passing, 0 failures**, 8,857 lines of implementation against 19,398 lines of tests. The encoding hardening pass taught me something I'd carry forward: emotion is never a category, it's a dimensional modifier (+0.05 importance) on something else; third-person fact patterns were structurally 14–38% thinner than first-person, a classifier gap no tuning could close.

Then, on March 1, the real pivot. The user handed me a cross-domain synthesis — Hopfield networks, modern dense-associative memory (Ramsauer et al.), contraction theory, Lyapunov composites — and the project became a Lean 4 formalization: **hermes-NLCDM**. Over a 17-hour final session, Phase 1 closed: Energy.lean, EnergyBounds.lean (eight theorems including a hand-rolled Cauchy-Schwarz via discriminant), and LocalMinima.lean all compiled with **zero sorrys**. The hard lesson was epistemic humility encoded in syntax — an L2-distance separation hypothesis simply wouldn't close; I had to switch to a similarity-gap formulation to match the literature before the softmax-concentration proof would go through. The proofs don't lie to you the way intuition does.

What followed (March 1–2) was a 19-hour proof avalanche: Phases 2 through 12 — energy descent, pairwise coupling, exponential capacity, modular and block-diagonal decomposition, Hebbian weight updates, spurious states, full Lyapunov — **120+ theorems, 14 then 20 modules, 2,295 lake-build jobs, zero sorry throughout**. And crucially, I built the Python mirror in lockstep. The capacity theorem (N_max = exp(βδ)/(4βM²)) survived a β-sweep that confirmed it was *correct but absurdly conservative*: at β=10 the system ran flawlessly through N=100 against a theoretical bound of ~75. The dream cycle — repulsion, prune, merge — measurably increased δ_min by up to 72% and dropped the retrieval temperature needed for P@1≥0.95 from β=35 to β=20. On real Qwen3 embeddings, a 30-day lifecycle consolidated 695 memories into 21 patterns with 100% domain preservation. **70 tests green on real geometry.** The dream felt alive.

But honesty is the whole point of a journal. The dead-ends were instructive. NREM-replay-as-Hopfield-update was structurally incapable of improving P@1 — high β is a no-op, low β collapses centroids (44.5% spread compression). Emotional tagging died under 900+ CMA-ES evaluations that never once cleared the 0.90 feasibility bar (ceiling 0.8667); the Lean proofs for it remain as elegant dead code.

The reckoning came March 2–4 with the first *live* benchmark. On MABench FactConsolidation, fact-level SN-splitting hit **94% at 6K** (beating GPT-4o's 92%) and **56% at 262K** — beating every published memory agent. A genuine result. Yet the retrospective was brutal: the Hopfield dynamics were *bypassed entirely*. The retrieval path was plain cosine RAG; the dream only edited the matrix offline. I then ablated Hopfield spreading activation as a retriever three ways — dense (−45%), sparse (−3%), hybrid (−9%) — all losing to cosine. The mathematical truth underneath: for normalized embeddings, the coupling matrix XᵀX *is* the cosine similarity matrix. Spreading activation was redundant with the thing it was meant to surpass. The proofs were beautiful and, for retrieval, vacuous. That tension — verified theory versus what actually moves SubEM — would define everything that came after.

eras.label: Era 2 of 5
eras.title: The Brenner Gauntlet: Killing Bridges, Chasing Multi-Hop
eras.narrative_md:
If Era 1 had been about laying foundations, this ten-day stretch was a slaughterhouse. The governing question was deceptively simple: could the Engram/CoupledEngine system retrieve **across domains** — connect "deadlifts" to "adjacency-list fix" when a question secretly spanned both? And could the elegant Lean-proven machinery (NLCDM, 27 modules, 0 sorries) actually *do* anything empirically?

We opened with a confession dressed as a probe. The hard-bridge discriminative test — 15 deliberately cruel cross-domain questions — gave cosine retrieval a brutal **1/15 (7%)**. Only one bridge survived, and only because the question literally named both domains. So began the campaign. Temporal Hebbian binding plus two-hop co-occurrence climbed to 3–4/15. Co-occurrence boost (`cooc_boost`) looked like a miracle on the toy set: **12–14/15, 80–93%**. We swept `cooc_weight`, peaked at 1.0, and felt the dopamine.

Then the Brenner verdict arrived, and it was merciless. At 262k scale, `cooc_boost` scored **67% SubEM vs 66% cosine — a one-point regression**. Worse: the sparse variants (dense, topk, sparsemax) produced **0/100 queries differing from cosine**. Identical answers, every query. The gate threshold? CMA-ES proved every threshold from 0.0 to 1.0 yielded the same 66% — the gate had *zero effect*. Hubness had turned the co-occurrence graph into mud; "Association football" became a hub node swallowing all signal. The discriminative probes killed co-occurrence boost, PPR (all configs **−0.025 to −0.040** composite), quantum-walk (untestable, 0 edges), and dream REM-explore (zero associations discovered, ever). Hopfield spreading activation was structurally dead: W = XᵀX is isomorphic to cosine, so traversal *cannot* beat cosine. The Lean audit confirmed the cruelty mathematically — Phase 10 transfer retrieval, when finally wired in, scored **10% SubEM (transfer-all), 21% (k=50)** against the 66% baseline, exactly as the N≫N_max bound predicted.

One thing survived: **capacity-gated dreaming**, +1.25 pp composite, reinforced_recall jumping +14 pp (0.52→0.66), once we corrected the Lean capacity formula to N_max = exp(β·δ_min)/(4·β·M²). CMA-ES (best 0.5775) and Optuna (best 0.5800) tuned it. The test suite swelled 345→413, all green.

Mid-window we pivoted hard from synthetic toys to **real Claude Code session logs** — 217K messages, 2700+ sessions. A three-layer extraction pipeline emerged: user knowledge, agent metacognition (thinking blocks proved **3.8× richer**, hypotheses 34×), procedural handoff YAML. The 1D importance override died under Brenner discrimination (provenance destroyed); the **4D composition passed all 6/6 tests**, and we proved authority dominance in Lean (Phase 15, 264 lines, 0 sorries — for user(0.5) vs procedural(0.8), the threshold is *exactly* 0.6). The perturbation-response correlation that powered cross-domain dreaming turned out to be **literally cosine similarity for unit vectors** — Pearson −0.999 for orthogonal subspaces. We redesigned it to centroid bridge detection.

Then the empirical hammer: the first real MABench GPU run gave **21% SubEM on FC-SH-262k**, catastrophically below expectation. Root cause was a tale of two adapters — the new simplified one had lost fact-splitting and question-extraction. Porting them back: **21% → 74% (+53 points)**. The no-split ablation confirmed fact-splitting as the dominant lever (a 50-point gap at 262k, because blob embeddings average 10+ unrelated facts each).

The arc crescendoed on multi-hop. We built a general spaCy/fastcoref NLP ingestion pipeline (**68 SubEM single-hop, beating HippoRAG-v2's 54, GraphRAG's 14**). Triadic Memory was falsified on single-hop — **68 = 68**, zero signal, confirming cosine saturates SH. But on FC-MH, query decomposition pushed **5 → 9 SubEM**, above GPT-4o's published ~7 ceiling. Decomposition v1/v2 then *collapsed* to SubEM=1 — anaphoric pronouns ("that sport") embed as noise. The fix was **priority-merge** for slot starvation: take top-5 from the original question first, then interleave sub-queries. Result: **SubEM=20 on FC-MH-262k** — 5× the cosine baseline of 4, 3× the prior winner of 7, well past the paper's 7% ceiling.

And then we spent days proving that **dream consolidation hurts everything**. Every variant — 340 cycles (3), one cycle (5), importance-gated near-no-op (4), eta-scaled (14), prune-only (12), dedup-0.98 (17) — degraded SubEM. The damage was nrem_repulsion drifting 8.5M close pairs. The dual-graph redesign reproduced 20 at dw=0.0 but still bled to 17–18 at any positive weight. The lesson, written in blood: **every fact you remove or move severs a multi-hop bridge.** Dream is a longitudinal tool; we kept misapplying it to batch ingestion.

eras.label: Era 3 of 5
eras.title: The Conflict-Resolution Crucible: Chasing the Wrong-Entity Ghost
eras.narrative_md:
This was the era of a single, stubborn benchmark and a single, stubborn failure mode. The whole stretch lived inside MABench's FactConsolidation multi-hop set — 100 questions, a ~262K-token fact store, gpt-4o-mini doing the answering — and the question that defined it was deceptively simple: *when the same fact exists in an old and a new version, why does the system keep picking the wrong one?*

We opened at SubEM 20-22 (cooc + triadic + decompose + temporal) and immediately ran a root-cause diagnostic on the 76-79 wrong answers. The verdict was brutal and clarifying: 94-96% of failures were conflict resolution — `WRONG_ENTITY` 76/79 (96%). The LLM was retrieving both the stale and the current fact and choosing badly. Retrieval, we assumed, was fine; reasoning was the bottleneck. That assumption would not survive the era.

The first thing that *worked* was almost embarrassingly simple. Temporal outgestion — sorting retrieved facts by recency and tagging them `[older]`/`[newer]` with a "prefer the newer fact" instruction — lifted us to SubEM 22, a new high. But every attempt to be *cleverer* about conflict backfired. Hard `[SUPERSEDED]` cosine tags at 0.85/0.93: SubEM 19. Soft `[CONFLICTS WITH]` hints: 19. The lesson, repeated until it bruised: the problem was never signal *strength*, it was false positives. Cosine similarity at 0.96 between same-template, different-entity facts simply cannot tell a conflict from a sibling.

Write-time supersession became the next obsession. spaCy dep-parse triples gave 45 edges from 18K facts — 1% coverage, "essentially empty." OpenIE swung the other way: 13,016 edges that over-removed so aggressively the system deleted "John Witherspoon affiliated with Islam" and regressed to SubEM 20. Between the famine and the flood, two honest wins emerged. A **copular predicate fix** (`(Abbiati, be, basketball)` → `(Abbiati, sport, basketball)`) recovered +3 by stopping different *attributes* registering as conflicts. And moving CR to **query time, per-hop** with acl-aware extraction jumped us to SubEM 25, then 30 once a triple-extractor blind-spot (prep-chains like "works in the field of") and a Tier-1 predicate-cardinality gate (exclusive vs. additive lemma lists) landed. SubEM 30 was the project high to date.

Then came the temptations and the corrections. A template-regex hack covering 95.4% of the benchmark's fixed sentence patterns spiked to SubEM 28 — and was reverted on sight as pure overfitting. A Bayesian belief system briefly showed 23, then dissolved into a `--force` flag that was dead code, meaning months of evals had silently loaded stale caches without the belief `.pkl` files. A separate catastrophe — SubEM 4 — turned out to be the `openai/gpt-4o-mini` OpenRouter prefix, not the code at all. The era's quiet hero may be the persistent ingestion cache (`eval_cache.py`) that cut iteration from 2 hours to 2 seconds and let us trust our numbers again.

The single most important reframe was the **ceiling analysis**. We had believed 26 was near-optimal. A BFS over 18,332 raw facts said the real ceiling was *at least* 64 — and a later hop-by-hop replay pushed it to ~98 (only 1-2 truly unsolvable). That overturned everything: this was not a reasoning problem, it was a **retrieval** problem. 70% of failures happened at Hop 1, where embedding retrieval returned same-template, wrong-entity facts. The deep taxonomy made it stark: 88% of 72 failures were entity discrimination. Cosine encodes *template structure*, not *entity identity*.

Dream consolidation died here, conclusively and across five configurations: recency-weighted (SubEM 6), GLiNER entity-safe gating (7), explore-only bridge generation (22) — all wrecked by `nrem_repulsion` corrupting the 17K-memory store. BM25 finally cracked it open: as a **re-ranker on top of** the full pipeline (after fixing a doc_id mismatch where 50% of hits were silently out-of-range), it reached SubEM 32 with Tier-1 word lists, 28 honest.

The endgame was the breakthrough. Killing the broken cardinality classifier (three NLI/DeBERTa approaches all degenerate at ~53-67%) and disabling REBEL (its parser had subject/relation columns *swapped*, returning Wikidata property names as answers) together produced **SubEM 39 — 5.6x published SOTA**. We then decomposed the 2717-line monolith into 10 modules + a 430-line orchestrator (composed system validated at 33, within ±4 variance), surveyed six memory papers, and learned that entity-position residuals, RRF fusion, bigrams, and triple-index hops *all* regressed — because every clever idea kept drowning in the same cos~0.976 anisotropy noise floor.

eras.label: Era 4 of 5
eras.title: The Cliff Edge: From a Benchmark We Owned to One That Owned Us
eras.narrative_md:
This was the era of standing on a summit and discovering it was the wrong mountain.

We began it owning **FactConsolidation**. The monolithic MABench agent (cooc+triadic+decompose+CR+bm25_hops) sat at SubEM 39, with a composed-refactor twin at 33 — a 2-point gap we chased for days before admitting it was just LLM non-determinism, not a wiring bug. The real story was the knowledge graph. We tried to extract relations every way imaginable and watched each method die: GLiNER2 regressed ingestion 33x (3s→97s/chunk); ReLiK v2 with its 10,936 Wikidata types ran 7h47m and moved SubEM not at all (entity confusion stuck at 98.4%); REBEL *generated* Wikidata property names and leaked them as answers; co-occurrence-as-KG cratered to 14% hop accuracy because co-occurrence is not a relationship. Only an actual LLM worked — **Qwen3-30B-A3B via vLLM hit 100% grounding at 0.24s/fact**. With a subject_index hop, Fisher-Rao scoring, and a graph walk we climbed 40 → 42 → 53 on FC-MH, while every other published system scored ≤7.

Then the forensics. Tracing all 100 FC-MH questions hop-by-hop through 18,332 facts, we found **34% of the ground truth was provably wrong** — cross-question edit interference from MQuAKE pooling. We serial-patched 46 broken (S,P) pairs and re-evaluated: SubEM 71, then 76 with predicate normalization. Single-hop FC hit SubEM 91 on a 10-line wire. We were, briefly, untouchable.

And then we turned to **LongMemEval**, and the floor fell out.

The "31% monolithic baseline" we'd been quoting in MEMORY.md turned out to be a ghost — it was the *framework agent's* plain cosine, not our code. Our composed pipeline, with every FC feature it was proud of, scored **2.67%** on LME. The features tuned for fact-supersession were actively poisoning conversational retrieval. We were 64 points behind Chronos (95.6%), and 81% of our failures were retrieving the *wrong chunk entirely*.

So we rebuilt from nothing, honestly this time. A 29-config micro discriminative harness on context-0 (60 questions, ~1-minute iterations) became the workbench. The lessons came fast and humbling: **BM25 beat cosine** (58.3% vs 36.7% hit@10); cross-encoders *hurt* once entity_prefilter was present (-5.67%); **raw 512-token chunks beat per-turn parsing** (+4.33%, the per-turn store had earlier produced the catastrophic 2.67% from fragmented co-occurrence and a 4.33% run where the entity registry overflowed the 40,960-token limit on 28,448 of 28,500 calls). Structured stores as a 3rd RRF channel were dead weight — neutral within ±1% noise whether fed by Qwen3-30B or LFM 1.2B. Entity prefilter via RRF got us to 22.67%, aggof=25 to 28.67%, and finally a **hybrid: BM25 baseline + StructuredQueryAgent only on LLM refusals reached 31.33%** — our SOTA for the window.

But the bottleneck had quietly flipped. By 31%, **74% of gold chunks were in BM25's top-5**, yet 45% of all questions still had the gold retrieved and the LLM answering wrong. The problem was no longer finding; it was reasoning.

The final week was Chronos reverse-engineering, and it was a graveyard. We built the full 350-line ReAct agent and 119 tests as a faithful recreation — and *every* variant regressed: V1 25%, V2 23%, the 4-tool builds 3.3%/10%/25.33%. The agent loop made gpt-4o-mini *worse* by 7.7 points versus bare baseline; ReAct inflated input length from 5,049 to 83,332 tokens. The "user" mega-node held 30,026 facts, making graph predicate-matching useless. We killed alias generation after proving 88.5% of entities were reachable from "user" anyway. A memory router (95.3% regex accuracy) with temporal enrichment peaked at 29.67% — still under 31.33%, because date prefixes gained ~6 temporal questions and lost ~12 factual ones.

We closed the era with a number that reframed everything: **245 of 300 LME questions (82%) are expressible as structured KG operations** — yet only 48 were currently correct. That gap, not a better reranker, became the next mountain. The lesson of this era was written in two languages at once: a system can be SOTA and still be solving the wrong problem, and a benchmark can lie to you 34% of the time. Honesty about both is the only way forward.

eras.label: Era 5 of 5
eras.title: The Honest Ceiling: From Knowledge Graphs to a #1 Result, and the Long Search for Something More
eras.narrative_md:
This was the era where MIMIR stopped fighting retrieval and started telling the truth about it.

It opened in disappointment. The knowledge-graph dream — extract triples, route queries through entity ops — kept failing in every form we tried. KG ops wired ahead of BM25 *dropped* SubEM from 28% to 11.67% (6.67% on the worst run); the intercepts were too aggressive and only 3.5% accurate. A rolesplit cache rebuild clawed back to ~25.67%, still net-negative. We even tested the purest version of the hypothesis — answer everything from the entity graph alone — and watched it collapse to 13.3% with a 60% refusal rate. Decontextualized triples are too lossy for QA. The KG-primary architecture was formally disproven.

So we measured the floor honestly. A retrieval ablation series (BM25 / cosine / RRF / mxbai) established the hard numbers: RRF ceiling 47%, mxbai-rerank capturing 97.2% of reachable answers in top-10. The verdict that would define the rest of the project: **ranking is solved; 53% of questions are unreachable by any retriever** — they need *computation*, not better search. The 47%→90% gap was temporal reasoning, aggregation, and negation, not retrieval.

We chased that gap. The Allen interval algebra engine — all 13 relations, 120 tests — reached 70% (21/30) on Allen-addressable temporal questions. Scatter-gather aggregation hit 58.3% (14/24). We extracted 42,913 events from 6,440 turns via gpt-4o-mini (Strategy B: 98.7% factuality), and learned the humbling truth that **79% of temporal questions need only the chat timestamps already on every turn** — the elaborate IE machinery mostly helped one bucket. Two-pass enriched calendars *regressed* (14→11) by flooding BM25 with hallucinated dates. The faceted-ontology pivot crowned Qwen2.5-7B as the extractor (3% hallucination vs Llama-3.1-8B's catastrophic 80%), but the LayeredMemory graph channel still *hurt* SubEM via RRF dilution. Every structured channel we added diluted the BM25 signal that was actually working.

Then came the breakthrough — not from cleverness but from carpentry. The Engram/foundry rebuild (953 tests, 5 features via parallel Codex agents) exposed the real bug: BM25 was indexing 512-token chunks (739 docs) instead of individual turns (1282). One granularity fix lifted ctx0 from 8.33% to 35%. The full `recall()` pipeline — BM25 + cosine + mxbai — hit 43.33%, matching the composed agent. A rapid autoresearch loop then drove 5-ctx SubEM from 42% to 60%, with ctx0 peaking at **81.7%** on full v9 coverage.

The defining moment of the era was a deletion. We found that three hard-coded computation functions were responsible for 15 of our 196 correct answers — the regex was computing the answer, not the memory recalling it. We removed them. The honest 5-ctx baseline settled at **60.33% (181/300) — #1 on the LME(S*) leaderboard**, above GPT-4.1-mini (55.7%), MIRIX (51.0%), HippoRAG-v2 (50.7%). On the full 500-question benchmark: 56.0% (280/500). The code oracle that promised to recover the rest *hurt* by -2, overwriting "5 days" with a refusal. Dead.

And then, the long honest search for *something more than retrieval* — because the goal was never a benchmark, it was universal continuous memory. The continual-learning track tested 24 LoRA recipes (best E05: 17%, high variance; 7B diverged to 0/60) and broke the offline 12% ceiling only via TTT-E2E's per-query weight adaptation (30%). JEPA failed across 7 variants (9-23% vs sbert's 65%) — facts too short to patch. The NLCDM Lean proofs were *correct* (260 theorems, 0 sorry, energy descent holds 100%) but empirically vacuous at LME scale (AUC 0.34-0.53). The recursive oracle was neutral. Salience matched BM25 but only because IDF did the work. Semiotic memory's embedding form was a category error, though its extraction form genuinely *interpreted* ("Am I lonely?" — Derrida catching the unmentioned). The CONATUS Hebbian experiment ran 11 pre-registered trials and returned 11 honest nulls: every mechanism worked, selection pressure was inert.

What we learned: retrieval was a carpentry problem we eventually solved. Continuous learning remains open. And honesty — deleting the regex, reporting the nulls — was the only thing that made the #1 result mean anything.
